all_candidates.g5_buyer: Software-supply-chain and build-attestation vendors (Chainguard, Sonatype, JFrog, Google Assured OSS) verifying that a published artifact matches its claimed build environment.
all_candidates.g6_note: Excellent. A .class file is typically 1-50KB and reduces to a compact structured feature sequence; a small model over constant-pool/attribute token sequences trains easily on 4 cores. Disk: download jars, extract per-class features, discard -- never hold the corpus. All four scales reachable.
all_candidates.input_modality: JVM bytecode: constant-pool ordering, attribute layout, synthetic-bridge generation, exception-table shape, StackMapTable encoding, local-variable slot allocation. Structured binary, only semi-legible.
all_candidates.name: Build-toolchain provenance from JVM bytecode at Maven Central scale
all_candidates.one_line: From .class bytecode alone, predict which compiler (javac vendor and point version, ecj, kotlinc), which build tool and which flags produced it -- with a 10^7-scale self-labelling corpus.
all_candidates.output_label: Compiler implementation + point version, build tool + plugin version, -source/-target, -g debug level, -parameters, shading/relocation, and whether the declared manifest provenance is a lie.

all_candidates.g1_corpus: Docker Hub hosts >8 million public images (Docker, Apr 2025). A published research dataset covers 3,364,529 Docker images with 378,615 corresponding git repositories. On the label side, >9.4 million unique Dockerfiles mined from GitHub 2013-2020 (the largest known Dockerfile dataset), plus the MSR 2020 dataset of ~178,000 parsed Dockerfiles.
all_candidates.g1_est_units: 8,000,000+ public images (Docker Hub, reported Apr 2025); 3,364,529 images in an existing research dataset (verified via literature); 9,400,000 unique Dockerfiles (verified via literature). Images retaining intact history metadata -- the labelled subset -- is >10^6 but the exact fraction is UNVERIFIED.
all_candidates.g2_mechanism: The image config JSON's history[] array stores created_by for every layer -- the literal Dockerfile command that produced it -- and the registry serves it for free with the manifest. Delete history[], squash the layers, and the (file-tree evidence -> instruction sequence) pair is manufactured at zero cost across millions of images. Complementary manufacturer: `docker build` the 9.4M mined Dockerfiles yourself, giving perfect pairs including for multi-stage builds whose history is genuinely unrecoverable from metadata.
all_candidates.g3_argument: The model input is a file tree of tens of thousands of (path, size, mode, mtime) tuples -- structured records, not documents. The mapping from 'these 4,000 files appeared with these modes' back to 'apt-get install -y build-essential' is a learned empirical prior over how package managers and base images touch the filesystem, and it improves monotonically as you cover more distros, package managers, language ecosystems and base images. No prompt encodes that prior.
all_candidates.g3_risk: Strongest kill, and it is severe: most public images still carry history metadata, so the answer is usually already in the artifact and the 'recovery' is a metadata read that dfimage/whaler do in 20 lines. For the squashed case, a frontier model handed just /var/lib/dpkg/status (or the top-level directory listing) will reconstruct the apt-get lines by plain reasoning, because Linux distributions helpfully write their own manifests to disk -- the filesystem is self-describing in exactly the way that kills a learned inverse. To survive, the task must target what is provably absent from metadata: multi-stage build structure, COPY source provenance, and instruction ORDER, which the community has documented as unrecoverable. That is a much narrower target. G4 check (searched 'Dockerfile reconstruction from container image machine learning'): only heuristic metadata dumpers -- dfimage, Whaler, dedockify, `docker history`. Zero ML work and no dataset for the inverse. Verified white space, but see the risk above for why.
all_candidates.g5_buyer: Container-security and SBOM vendors (Chainguard, Sysdig, Aqua, Docker Scout) that must establish provenance for imported third-party or squashed images.
all_candidates.g6_note: Training is genuinely cheap -- a file tree compresses to a short token sequence of path-prefix/mode/size buckets, and a small seq2seq model on 4 cores handles 10^6 of them. The real risk is ACQUISITION, not training: pulling 10^6 image layer blobs is many TB against 30GB of disk, so you must stream tar listings and discard blobs immediately, or restrict to manifest+listing endpoints. Budget the crawl, not the GPU.
all_candidates.input_modality: Structured records, not prose: per-layer file trees of (path, size, mode, uid/gid, mtime, hash prefix, whiteout markers) and inter-layer diffs.
all_candidates.name: Container image to build-instruction recovery from filesystem evidence
all_candidates.one_line: From a squashed container image's file-tree evidence alone -- no history metadata -- reconstruct the sequence of Dockerfile instructions that built it.
all_candidates.output_label: Ordered sequence of instruction types (FROM/RUN/COPY/ADD/ENV/WORKDIR) with argument skeletons: base-image identity, package-manager invocations and package sets, COPY destinations, build-stage boundaries.

all_candidates.g1_corpus: Not an existing corpus -- generated. Feedstock is public HDL: millions of .v/.vhd files across GitHub and Software Heritage (27B files), plus OpenCores, LiteX and the CHIPS Alliance repos. Open bit-documentation databases (Project X-Ray for Xilinx 7-series, Project Trellis for ECP5, Project IceStorm for iCE40) plus fasm2bels define the label space; yosys+nextpnr generate pairs.
all_candidates.g1_est_units: Existing public (bitstream, netlist) corpora at 10^6 scale: none -- UNVERIFIED and almost certainly non-existent. Generated pairs: reachable to ~10^5 small designs on a 4-core box (see g6), with each design yielding thousands of tile-level units, so 10^7 tile units is plausible from 10^4-10^5 P&R runs.
all_candidates.g2_mechanism: The place-and-route tool is the oracle: you synthesised the netlist, so you know it exactly. yosys -> nextpnr -> icepack/ecppack produces (netlist, bitstream) pairs with perfect ground truth and no human. Randomising the source HDL and the P&R seed produces unlimited label diversity.
all_candidates.g3_argument: The input is a bit array with no textual structure whatsoever; a frontier model cannot represent it and prompting is not expressible. Scale helps because the bit-to-feature mapping is a large, sparse, device-specific lookup that must be learned from correlations, and coverage of rare tile types (DSP, BRAM, clocking) only comes from many designs.
all_candidates.g3_risk: Strongest kill is not a language model at all -- it is a fuzzer. Project X-Ray's differential-fuzzing method solves this mapping EXACTLY for any family you can run the vendor tool on, and exact beats learned every time. So a learned model only matters for families where you cannot fuzz, and for those families you also cannot generate training labels -- the moat and the data source are the same wall. That circularity is close to fatal. Secondary: bitstream encryption on modern parts removes the input entirely. G4 check (searched 'FPGA bitstream reverse engineering machine learning netlist recovery'): the space has many efforts but almost all deterministic -- Debit, BIL, Bit2ncd, fasm2bels, plus the 2026 'SoK: From Silicon to Netlist and Beyond' survey; ML appears only for coarse IP-core identification from bitstream-as-image. Arguably >3 serious efforts overall, so G4 is BORDERLINE at best. Listing this for completeness, not as a front-runner.
all_candidates.g5_buyer: Hardware IP-protection and anti-counterfeiting vendors, plus defence/aerospace supply-chain assurance labs verifying that a fielded FPGA carries the netlist it is supposed to.
all_candidates.g6_note: Marginal, and I want to be precise: the MODEL trains fine on CPU (bit windows, small conv net). The DATA does not scale freely -- nextpnr place-and-route is seconds-to-minutes per design, so ~10^5 tiny iCE40/ECP5 designs is roughly a full day of 4-core wall time and 10^6 is out of reach. Also the scientifically interesting families (UltraScale, Intel) need proprietary tools whose EULAs make bulk scripted generation legally awkward and whose memory footprint exceeds 15GB. Feasible only in the open-toolchain corner, which is the corner where the problem is already solved.
all_candidates.input_modality: Raw FPGA configuration bitstream bits, addressed by frame/tile coordinates. About as far from web text as any modality gets.
all_candidates.name: FPGA bitstream to LUT/route configuration recovery
all_candidates.one_line: Learn the inverse of place-and-route: map raw configuration bits back to LUT init values, flip-flop settings and routing multiplexer choices.
all_candidates.output_label: Per-tile FASM-style feature set: LUT INIT vectors, FF/latch configuration, routing PIPs enabled, BRAM/DSP mode bits -- i.e. a recovered gate-level netlist.

all_candidates.g1_corpus: Public HDL as feedstock: millions of .v/.vhd files on GitHub and in Software Heritage (27B files, 421M projects); OpenCores, LiteX, CHIPS Alliance, the OpenROAD/OpenLane benchmark suites. Open PDK cell libraries (SkyWater sky130, GF180) supply real technology targets, and Yosys+ABC supply the flows.
all_candidates.g1_est_units: Existing public (netlist, synthesis-recipe) datasets: none at any scale -- UNVERIFIED/non-existent. Generated: each HDL module x each recipe is one unit, and yosys synth of a small module is ~0.1-1s, so 10^6 units is 1-3 CPU-days on 4 cores -- reachable but at the edge.
all_candidates.g2_mechanism: You ran the synthesiser, so you know the recipe. Sample an HDL module, sample a random point in the recipe space (tool pass order, effort, library, flag vector), run yosys/ABC, record the netlist. Perfect labels, no human, and the recipe space is yours to design so you can deliberately create near-degenerate pairs that force the model to find subtle structural fingerprints rather than gross size cues.
all_candidates.g3_argument: A netlist is a graph of anonymous cells; a frontier model cannot ingest a 200k-instance graph and there is no prose to prompt against. The claim that scales is that synthesis flows leave a structural signature -- characteristic gate-mix ratios, buffer-tree shapes, register-retiming footprints, cell-choice idioms -- and separating flows that differ by one flag is a statistical discrimination problem that improves with corpus size and with library diversity.
all_candidates.g3_risk: Strongest kill: the tech-library name is often literally in the cell names (sky130_fd_sc_hd__nand2_1), so a chunk of the label is a regex away, and a frontier model reading the first fifty lines of the netlist file as text would get the library and probably the tool. To be a real task the netlist must be presented anonymised (cells renamed to generic types), which is defensible but a reviewer will call it artificial. Second risk: does anyone need this? The buyer story is IP-provenance litigation, which is small and slow. G4 check (searched 'synthesis tool script technology library provenance from gate-level netlist' and 'gate-level netlist reverse engineering word-level structure ML'): the ADJACENT problem -- functional/word-level netlist RE -- is genuinely crowded (HAL, WordRev, ReIGNN, ABGNN, equality-saturation methods, the 2026 hardware-RE SoK), so do NOT propose that framing. Synthesis-RECIPE provenance specifically returned no research at all, only tool-flow documentation. White space verified for the provenance framing; the neighbouring functional-recovery framing is full.
all_candidates.g5_buyer: Semiconductor IP-licensing and litigation-support firms, plus fabless supply-chain assurance teams checking that a delivered netlist came from the flow the contract specified.
all_candidates.g6_note: Feasible with care. Restrict to small modules (<5k cells) so yosys runs in ~0.1-0.5s and the graph fits a small GNN or a linearised-token transformer on 4 cores. 10^6 units is 1-3 CPU-days of generation -- do the 1k/10k/100k scales first and only push to 1M if the curve is already bending the right way. Netlists compress well; 30GB is enough if you store features, not Verilog.
all_candidates.input_modality: Structured directed graphs (cell instances, nets, fanout cones) -- a netlist graph, not text and not an image.
all_candidates.name: Synthesis-recipe provenance from gate-level netlists
all_candidates.one_line: Given only a gate-level netlist, recover the synthesis flow that produced it: tool, script, technology library, effort level, retiming/resource-sharing/flattening flags.
all_candidates.output_label: Synthesis tool + version, standard-cell library family, optimisation effort, and the flag set (retiming on/off, resource sharing, flattening, clock-gating insertion, DFT insertion).

all_candidates.g1_corpus: Generated, from freely available software: dump the address space of processes built from Debian's 64,419 packages (or any distro), each with matching DWARF from the debug archives; kernel dumps from distro kernels with debuginfod symbols. Existing public dump collections are small and mostly CTF-scale.
all_candidates.g1_est_units: Public labelled memory-dump datasets at 10^6 scale: none -- UNVERIFIED/non-existent. But the unit is an OBJECT, not a dump: a single medium process image contains 10^5-10^6 live objects, so ~10-100 dumps already give 10^6+ labelled units and a few thousand dumps give 10^8.
all_candidates.g2_mechanism: Debug symbols plus the allocator are the label manufacturer. Run a binary that still has DWARF/PDB, snapshot its memory, and use the symbol tables plus allocator metadata (or an LD_PRELOAD shim recording every malloc/free with its call site and static type) to emit exact object boundaries and types. Then discard the symbols and keep the raw bytes. Zero human labelling; the same trick as VPT's inverse model, except the 'inverse model' is a debugger you already own.
all_candidates.g3_argument: The input is undifferentiated memory bytes and a pointer graph; there is nothing to prompt. The learnable prior -- what a std::vector header looks like, how a slab-allocated struct is aligned, what a vtable pointer neighbourhood looks like -- is empirical and improves with more programs, more compilers and more allocators. Critically it degrades gracefully across kernel/library versions, which is exactly where profile-based tooling breaks completely; that fragility is the commercial pain.
all_candidates.g3_risk: Strongest kill: when the profile matches, Volatility/rekall parse memory exactly and for free, and a frontier model with a Volatility MCP tool is strictly better than any learned detector. For the profile-mismatch case, pool-tag and allocator-metadata heuristics already recover most Windows/Linux kernel objects, which is why DeepMem (CCS 2018) demonstrated gains and then saw essentially no adoption -- a warning sign that the pain is not as acute as the pitch. Also the eval is awkward: your ground truth comes from symbols, so you can only test on binaries that have symbols, which are not the binaries the customer cares about. G4 check (searched 'memory dump kernel object structure recovery deep learning profile-free'): DeepMem (CCS'18, GNN) and the Eurecom 'zero-knowledge approach to memory forensics' are the two serious efforts, plus older heuristic work on dynamic kernel-structure recreation. Under 3 efforts, no open dataset at scale. White space verified; adoption history is the caution.
all_candidates.g5_buyer: DFIR and EDR vendors (Volexity, Magnet Forensics, CrowdStrike) whose memory-analysis profiles break on every kernel and glibc update.
all_candidates.g6_note: Training is fine: units are small byte neighbourhoods plus local graph features, and a small model on 4 cores handles 10^6 objects. Generate USERSPACE process dumps (gcore on small binaries), not VM snapshots -- full VM memory images are GBs each and would blow the 30GB disk. A few hundred process dumps, streamed and featurised, cover all four scales.
all_candidates.input_modality: Raw memory bytes plus the derived pointer graph (candidate pointers, alignment, allocator metadata). No text.
all_candidates.name: Profile-free object and type layout recovery from memory images
all_candidates.one_line: From raw process or kernel memory bytes, locate allocated objects, recover their struct types and field layouts without any version-matched profile.
all_candidates.output_label: Object start offsets, struct type label, field boundaries and field types, allocation state.

all_candidates.g1_corpus: Manufactured from every ELF/PE binary that exists: Debian bookworm's 64,419 packages across ~8 architectures, the Assemblage corpus (428,884 Linux ELF + 890,000 Windows PE binaries, arXiv 2405.03991), plus Software Heritage's 27B files as source for cross-compiled targets, plus real vendor firmware images for held-out evaluation.
all_candidates.g1_est_units: 428,884 ELF + 890,000 PE binaries (Assemblage, verified via literature) directly convertible into labelled headerless blobs -- already >10^6 units before any cross-compilation. Cross-compiling to 20+ architectures multiplies this arbitrarily.
all_candidates.g2_mechanism: The header IS the label, so you manufacture the task by deleting it. Take any ELF/PE, read its true load address, entry point, architecture and section table, then strip all headers and optionally relocate the image to a random base -- you now have a headerless blob whose every answer you know exactly. Cost: one pyelftools read plus one memcpy per unit. This is the cleanest label manufacturer in this whole list: the labels already exist in 10^6+ artefacts and the corpus is fully public.
all_candidates.g3_argument: Base-address recovery is a global inverse over the whole blob: the correct base is the one under which the largest number of embedded 32/64-bit words become valid pointers into strings, code and tables. That is a statistical alignment problem over raw bytes with no prompt formulation, no text, and no context window that holds 8MB. Scaling is monotone and testable: coverage of more architectures, more ABIs, more compiler pointer-emission idioms strictly improves generalisation to an unseen vendor blob, and RISC-V/Xtensa/ARC style long-tail ISAs are exactly where existing tools have nothing.
all_candidates.g3_risk: Strongest kill: the existing heuristics are simple and work. rbasefind, basefind.py and Quarkslab's binbloom v2 brute-force the base by counting string/pointer intersections, and an agentic frontier model that shells out to binbloom gets the answer without learning anything. The honest defence is where those tools are documented to fail -- 64-bit firmware (rbasefind explicitly does not support it), blobs with too few strings, position-independent images with no absolute pointers, and packed/compressed regions -- but a reviewer will fairly ask what fraction of real firmware that is. Second risk: relocating a stripped ELF to a random base is not perfectly faithful to how real headerless blobs are built (real ones were compiled for their base), so a domain gap may make the impressive training numbers evaporate on vendor firmware; the eval must be on real held-out blobs. G4 check (searched 'firmware base address determination headerless blob rbasefind machine learning'): only heuristic tools -- rbasefind, basefind.py/.cpp, binbloom v2, plus open feature requests in rizin and radare2. Zero ML approaches, zero datasets. Verified white space, and the open tool-tracker issues are direct evidence of unmet demand.
all_candidates.g5_buyer: Firmware reverse-engineering and IoT security platforms (ONEKEY, NetRise, Binary Ninja/Hex-Rays tooling vendors) whose analysts currently guess base addresses by hand before any analysis can start.
all_candidates.g6_note: Best G6 profile in this list. Labels are manufactured from existing binaries at ~milliseconds each with no compilation, no synthesis, no VM. Units are byte windows plus a compact pointer-histogram feature vector; a small model trains on 4 cores. All four scales (1k/10k/100k/1M) come from the Assemblage corpus alone, and you can stream-and-discard so 30GB of disk is ample.
all_candidates.input_modality: Raw byte stream plus derived pointer-value histograms and instruction-alignment statistics. No headers, no metadata, no text.
all_candidates.name: Load-layout recovery for headerless firmware blobs
all_candidates.one_line: Given a raw firmware blob with no ELF/PE header, recover its load base address, architecture, endianness, entry point and code/data section boundaries.
all_candidates.output_label: Base address (the hard one), ISA + endianness + word size, entry point, and per-offset code/data/rodata/string-table segmentation.

all_candidates.g1_corpus: Argo Global Data Assembly Centres (GDAC), free and unrestricted: https://argo.ucsd.edu/data/ ; ftp/https mirrors at Ifremer and US-GODAE. Every profile NetCDF file carries BOTH the raw PARAM and the expert PARAM_ADJUSTED/PARAM_ADJUSTED_ERROR plus QC flags. Verified: 'Argo Data 1999-2019: Two Million Temperature-Salinity Profiles' (Front. Mar. Sci. 2020) https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/marine-science/articles/10.3389/fmars.2020.00700/full ; fleet is ~4,000 floats adding 100,000+ profiles/yr; a published DMQC study analysed 10,048 floats.
all_candidates.g1_est_units: ~2.0e6 core profiles verified as of 2019, ~3e6 today including BGC-Argo; ~1.5e4 distinct float instruments. Profiles are 1-10 KB each, so a 1e6-profile subset is a few GB.
all_candidates.g2_mechanism: The archive is already a paired corpus and nobody has used it as one: twenty years of human DMQC operators have written the corrected answer next to the raw measurement inside every file. Downloading the GDAC yields (raw profile + trajectory context -> expert correction) pairs at exactly the cost of bandwidth. Secondary free truth: the OWC/climatology reference comparison and ship-based CTD crossovers can be recomputed offline with open code (pyowc) to densify labels for profiles not yet in delayed mode.
all_candidates.g3_argument: The task is a per-instrument inverse calibration where the signal is ~0.01 PSU hidden under real ocean variability, so performance depends on how much regional hydrography and how many drift trajectories the model has internalised - a textbook data-scaling curve. The input is a numeric profile; there is no prompt that expresses 'here are 900 float levels, infer the conductivity cell drift'. Delayed-mode currently lags real-time by ~1 year of human labour, so a learned inverse has an operational reason to exist independent of model size.
all_candidates.g3_risk: Strongest attack: the operational DMQC adjustment is mostly a slowly-varying offset estimated against a reference climatology by weighted least squares (OWC), which is already the accepted standard and may be near the information ceiling; the labels themselves are inconsistent human judgements across DACs, so you would be fitting expert noise, and 90% of floats need no adjustment in their first two years, making the positive class rare. A frontier model with a code interpreter does not need to 'know' anything - it just runs pyowc.
all_candidates.g5_buyer: Ocean sensor manufacturers (Sea-Bird Scientific, RBR) certifying in-service accuracy, and operational forecasting centres (Mercator Ocean, ECMWF, NOAA/NCEP) that currently pay expert-hours per float for delayed-mode QC.
all_candidates.g6_note: Ideal for CPU: profiles are small numeric arrays; a 1k/10k/100k/1M profile ladder fits easily in 30 GB if you download a stratified subset of the GDAC rather than the whole archive. A 1-5M-param sequence model over 1000-level profiles trains in hours on 4 cores.
all_candidates.input_modality: Numeric vertical profile arrays (pressure/temperature/conductivity at 70-1000 levels) plus the float's own cycle history and neighbouring-float context. Pure float vectors, no text.
all_candidates.name: Argo float CTD calibration inversion (real-time profile -> delayed-mode adjusted profile)
all_candidates.one_line: Learn the expert delayed-mode QC transform that converts a raw autonomous-float temperature/salinity profile into a calibrated one, i.e. an inverse sensor-drift model for a 4,000-instrument global fleet.
all_candidates.output_label: Per-profile calibration correction: salinity offset + time-drift slope, pressure offset, thermal-lag (CTM) coefficients, plus the per-level QC flag vector (PSAL_ADJUSTED - PSAL and its error).

all_candidates.g1_corpus: Coherent X-ray Imaging Data Bank (CXIDB) https://www.cxidb.org/browse.html - open deposits, notably CXIDB ID 185, 'A multi-million image Serial Femtosecond Crystallography dataset collected at the European XFEL', Sci. Data 2022 https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-022-01266-w (~19 million images, HDF5, released explicitly for algorithm development). Plus dozens of other SFX/SSX deposits, and Crystallography Open Database https://www.crystallography.net/cod/ (verified 534,680 entries, 2026-08) for unlimited simulated peak lists.
all_candidates.g1_est_units: ~1.9e7 real diffraction snapshots in CXIDB ID 185 alone (verified); ~5.3e5 known crystal structures for simulation, giving effectively unbounded synthetic peak lists.
all_candidates.g2_mechanism: (b) Run the existing free indexers (CrystFEL with XGANDALF/MOSFLM/TORO, DIALS) over the archive: every pattern they DO index becomes a free (peak list -> A-matrix) pair, at CPU cost only, with no human in the loop - this is the exact VPT move, using the classical algorithm as the contractor. (c) For the failure tail, forward-simulate peak lists from COD/PDB cells with sampled orientation, mosaicity, partiality, detector gaps and shot noise - the artifact was generated from a structured source that still exists.
all_candidates.g3_argument: Indexing rate is the literal throughput bottleneck of serial crystallography: facilities discard the majority of hits. Classical indexers are per-pattern combinatorial searches that cannot amortise anything across a run; a learned indexer accumulates priors over cells, orientations and detector pathologies, so more patterns and more compute monotonically raise the indexing yield. Prompting a text model with a list of 40 pixel coordinates is not a coherent operation.
all_candidates.g3_risk: Strongest attack: indexing is a well-posed geometric problem, and when XGANDALF fails it usually fails because the pattern genuinely lacks information (too few peaks, overlapping lattices, bad geometry) - no amount of learned prior manufactures the missing constraint. TORO already indexes at kHz using GPU-style batching, so the speed argument is gone, and a frontier model asked to 'index this' will simply call CrystFEL, which is the correct answer.
all_candidates.g5_buyer: XFEL and synchrotron facilities (European XFEL, LCLS, SwissFEL, Diamond, SACLA) whose scarce resource is beamtime per solved structure, and structural-biology CROs/pharma running serial rooms for fragment screening.
all_candidates.g6_note: Feasible ONLY on peak lists, not raw frames: CXIDB 185 raw is ~100 TB, far beyond 30 GB. Use the peak arrays already stored inside CXI files (/entry/result/peakXPosRaw) or simulate peak lists directly from COD cells - a few hundred bytes per pattern, so 1e6 patterns is well under 1 GB. Set transformer over point sets, trivially CPU-trainable at 4 scales.
all_candidates.input_modality: Unordered 2D point sets: 15-200 Bragg peak (x, y, intensity) tuples per snapshot plus detector geometry. Point-cloud geometry, categorically outside web-text distribution.
all_candidates.name: Serial-crystallography indexing from Bragg peak lists
all_candidates.one_line: Learn to index sparse diffraction snapshots - map an unordered set of Bragg peak coordinates to a unit cell and orientation matrix - for the 50-80% of serial femtosecond crystallography patterns that classical indexers throw away.
all_candidates.output_label: The 3x3 orientation/lattice matrix A (equivalently unit cell a,b,c,alpha,beta,gamma + rotation), or the 'unindexable' class; optionally multi-lattice decomposition.

all_candidates.g1_corpus: Public model repositories: Printables https://www.printables.com (~1.5M free models by 2026) and Thingiverse https://www.thingiverse.com (2.5M+ officially, ~7M by model ID). Open slicers that act as the label generator: PrusaSlicer, OrcaSlicer, CuraEngine (all GPL, headless CLI). Prior art on the corpus side: 'Thirty Thousand 3D Models from Thingiverse', Data 2018 https://www.mdpi.com/2306-5729/3/1/5
all_candidates.g1_est_units: >=1.5e6 downloadable meshes on Printables alone (verified); Thingiverse adds several million more. Each mesh x sampled config = one unit, so the corpus is effectively unbounded above 1e6.
all_candidates.g2_mechanism: Every G-code file in the world was generated by a deterministic open-source program from (mesh, config). Run PrusaSlicer/CuraEngine headless over the mesh corpus with randomly sampled configuration vectors: each invocation costs seconds of CPU and emits an exactly-labelled (G-code, full config, layer polygons) triple. Strip the slicer's own comment header, which otherwise leaks the answer. This is the FDM-1 move with the slicer standing in for the contractor-trained IDM.
all_candidates.g3_argument: The target is a 40-dim continuous configuration plus geometry recovered from a 1e5-token numeric path - the mapping is many-to-one and genuinely learned. Coverage over mesh topology x parameter space is what improves it, so scale is the lever. It transfers to the real question (an unlabelled .gcode from an unknown farm) which no metadata can answer. A language model cannot ingest 100k coordinate lines meaningfully.
all_candidates.g3_risk: Strongest and honest attack: a large fraction of the parameter vector is recoverable by a 20-line deterministic script - layer height is the Z delta, temperature is literally M104, acceleration is M204, extrusion width follows from E per unit distance divided by layer height. A frontier model that writes that script beats a trained network on most of the vector, and the genuinely hidden residual (infill pattern class, slicer identity, seam strategy) may be a small, low-value subset. The study must be framed on the residual, not on the whole vector, or it dies here.
all_candidates.g5_buyer: Additive-manufacturing service bureaus and printer OEMs (Bambu Lab, Prusa Research, Stratasys, Ultimaker) doing print-failure forensics and part qualification; also aerospace/medical AM supply chains that must prove process traceability for a delivered part.
all_candidates.g6_note: Fully CPU-feasible but disk-bound: G-code is verbose (10-500 MB per large model). Cap mesh size, slice a stratified subset, and store tokenised/binary paths. 1k/10k/100k/1M sliced parts is achievable if you truncate to the first N layers per part.
all_candidates.input_modality: Numeric motion-command token streams (G1 X/Y/Z/E/F, M-codes) of 1e4-1e6 lines with all metadata comments stripped. Coordinate soup, not prose.
all_candidates.name: Slicer inversion: recovering process parameters and layer geometry from FFF G-code
all_candidates.one_line: Given a comment-stripped 3D-printer toolpath, recover the ~40-dimensional slicer configuration and the sliced geometry that produced it - an inverse slicer for additive manufacturing forensics and traceability.
all_candidates.output_label: Slicer identity and version + the process-parameter vector (layer height, nozzle/extrusion width, infill density and pattern, perimeter count, print/travel speeds, acceleration, jerk, retraction, temperatures, cooling) and the per-layer contour polygons of the source mesh.

all_candidates.g1_corpus: Public KiCad/Altium hardware projects on GitHub/GitLab (github.com/topics/kicad-pcb, kicad, gerber-files) whose repositories contain BOTH the fabrication outputs and the source design; KiCad CLI (kicad-cli pcb export gerbers) as the plotting engine; freerouting + KiCad for unbounded synthetic board generation. CROWDING CHECK PERFORMED: searches surface only commercial CAM workflows (Altium CAMtastic, Numerical Innovations, reversepcb.com) and X-ray/imaging-based PCB reverse engineering - I found NO ML dataset or learned model for Gerber -> schematic semantics.
all_candidates.g1_est_units: UNVERIFIED for real-world Gerbers - I could not establish a >=1e6 count of public board designs and will not invent one. The manufacturable route (sample netlists, auto-place/auto-route, plot Gerbers) is unbounded and >=1e6 is trivially reachable, but that is synthesis, not an existing corpus. Treat G1 as PARTIAL.
all_candidates.g2_mechanism: Gerbers are a lossy projection of a structured source (.kicad_pcb + schematic + BOM) that still exists in the repo. Running KiCad's plotter over each project regenerates the fabrication package while the project file supplies refdes, values, net names, net classes and connectivity - free, exact labels. The same pipeline run over synthesised boards gives unlimited additional pairs.
all_candidates.g3_argument: The model input is planar copper geometry; there is no prompt formulation of 'here are 80,000 aperture flashes, tell me which net is 3V3'. Layout idiom priors (decoupling placement, star grounds, USB differential pairs, thermal reliefs) are exactly the kind of statistical regularity that improves with corpus breadth across board classes.
all_candidates.g3_risk: Strongest attack: net CONNECTIVITY is already deterministically extractable by mature CAM tools, so the learned part reduces to component semantics - and component value is often physically undetermined by copper alone (two identical 0402 pads can be 100nF or 1nF), meaning the ceiling is set by missing information, not by compute. Worse, a frontier vision model handed a rendered board with silkscreen refdes and outlines would likely recover most of the semantics with zero training, and the highest-value real-world case (a physical board, not a Gerber) is an imaging problem anyway.
all_candidates.g5_buyer: Electronics supply-chain assurance and counterfeit-detection labs serving defense primes (the DARPA/CAD-for-Assurance ecosystem), plus EMS houses and repair/refurb operations quoting or servicing boards with no design package.
all_candidates.g6_note: Compact: Gerber primitives serialise to short numeric token sequences; a board is kilobytes to a few MB. Generating 1e5-1e6 synthetic boards with freerouting is the CPU cost, and routing is the slow step - budget it, or cap board size at ~50 components.
all_candidates.input_modality: RS-274X aperture/flash/draw geometry primitives and NC-drill coordinates per layer - 2D vector polygon soup, tens to hundreds of thousands of primitives per board. Not natural language, not a natural image.
all_candidates.name: Gerber-to-schematic: recovering design intent from PCB fabrication data
all_candidates.one_line: Given only the copper geometry and drill data a factory receives, recover component identities, values and net semantics - i.e. reconstruct the schematic a board was built from.
all_candidates.output_label: Per-footprint component class and value bucket (100nF decoupling cap vs 10uF bulk vs crystal vs FET), net semantic roles (power rail and nominal voltage, ground, differential pair, clock, high-current), and the schematic-level connectivity graph.

all_candidates.g1_corpus: NREL SMART-DS synthetic distribution models on OEDI/data.gov: https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981 - 2,711 feeders covering the greater San Francisco Bay Area, Greensboro NC and Austin TX, with OpenDSS models, geojson, and connected time-series loads, documented as covering 'millions of customers' with complete ground-truth topology. Real unlabelled AMI for transfer: Low Carbon London (5,567 households), Pecan Street, Smart Grid Smart City (AU).
all_candidates.g1_est_units: >=1e6 customer-level load/voltage series in SMART-DS (verified: 'up to hundreds of feeders and millions of customers'; 2,711 feeders across three metros). Real labelled AMI is orders of magnitude smaller - low 1e4 households.
all_candidates.g2_mechanism: OpenDSS is the free oracle. Running power flow over the published synthetic networks with sampled load/DER/measurement-noise scenarios yields unlimited (voltage series -> exact phase, transformer assignment, topology) pairs at pure CPU cost, because the simulator knows the answer by construction. Utility GIS records provide a small, noisy real-world seed for domain transfer.
all_candidates.g3_argument: Correlation-and-clustering heuristics degrade badly as rooftop PV, EVs and heat pumps decorrelate voltage profiles - the regime is getting harder, not easier. A learned model amortises across thousands of feeder topologies rather than solving each feeder from scratch, and coverage across cities/feeder archetypes is exactly what scale buys. No prompt expresses a year of 15-minute voltages for 3,000 meters.
all_candidates.g3_risk: Strongest attack: with enough samples, phase identification is largely solved by voltage-correlation plus spectral clustering, and utilities already buy it from AMI vendors - so the marginal value of a learned model is thin. Worse, the corpus is SYNTHETIC: if OpenDSS scenarios do not reproduce real meter noise, clock skew, and missing reads, the sim-to-real gap caps performance and more synthetic data makes it worse, not better. That is a scaling curve that bends the wrong way.
all_candidates.g5_buyer: Electric utilities and AMI head-end vendors (Itron, Landis+Gyr, Sensus) selling grid-model validation and DER hosting-capacity analysis, where a wrong phase label directly blocks interconnection approvals.
all_candidates.g6_note: CPU-friendly - the units are short numeric series and small graphs. The real cost is running OpenDSS to generate scenarios, which is CPU-bound but parallelisable across 4 cores; pre-generate 1e6 meter-windows once (a few GB) and train at 4 scales from that.
all_candidates.input_modality: Multivariate numeric voltage/kWh time series (15-min or hourly), 1e3-1e5 correlated series per feeder. Telemetry, no text anywhere.
all_candidates.name: Distribution-grid phase and topology inversion from meter voltage series
all_candidates.one_line: Infer the physical low-voltage network - which phase each customer is on, which transformer they hang off, and the feeder impedances - from nothing but smart-meter voltage time series.
all_candidates.output_label: Per-meter phase label (A/B/C), meter-to-service-transformer assignment, feeder connectivity edges and per-segment impedance estimates.

all_candidates.g1_corpus: NESO (National Grid ESO) Data Portal, open licence: System Frequency at 1-second resolution from January 2020 (https://www.neso.energy / data.neso.energy, mirrored at https://opennetzero.org/national-grid-eso/system-frequency-data), plus the System Inertia dataset and 5-minute generation-by-fuel outturn on the same clock. Comparable open feeds from EirGrid, Fingrid, and ENTSO-E Transparency.
all_candidates.g1_est_units: ~2e8 one-second frequency samples for Great Britain since 2020 (verified 1-s resolution, from Jan 2020) => ~3e5 ten-minute windows per TSO-decade; pooling several TSOs and using overlapping windows puts the unit count comfortably above 1e6.
all_candidates.g2_mechanism: The operator publishes the answer next to the question. NESO releases its outturn inertia estimate and the settlement-grade generation mix on the same timeline as the raw frequency trace, so a temporal join manufactures labelled (waveform window -> inertia, mix) pairs retroactively for six years at zero marginal cost. Physics simulators (swing equation / OpenModelica grid models) can densify the rare large-disturbance tail.
all_candidates.g3_argument: The map from frequency fine structure to the machine inventory behind it is non-analytic and event-driven; the informative moments are rare disturbances, so more years and more TSOs strictly help - a textbook data-constrained regime. The input is a waveform: plain prompting cannot even be phrased, let alone compete.
all_candidates.g3_risk: Strongest attack: a serious incumbent already exists - GE Vernova sells NESO an Effective Inertia Metering and Forecasting product and NESO has deployed ML-based inertia forecasting. And the label is itself a model output (NESO's own inertia estimate), so a learned model is distilling somebody else's heuristic and is capped by it; true inertia is never observed. A frontier model with the published mix data can also just apply textbook per-technology inertia constants and get most of the way there.
all_candidates.g5_buyer: Transmission system operators that procure stability/inertia services (NESO, EirGrid, Fingrid, AEMO), plus battery and synchronous-condenser operators bidding into those inertia markets who need independent measurement.
all_candidates.g6_note: Trivially CPU-feasible: a 10-minute 1 Hz window is 600 floats. The entire GB frequency archive is a few GB of CSV. Four scales from 1k to 1M windows is easy; the constraint is label diversity (only ~6 years x a handful of TSOs), not compute.
all_candidates.input_modality: 1 Hz (and sub-second where published) frequency waveform and derived ROCOF - a scalar time series with rich transient structure. Waveform, not text.
all_candidates.name: Grid frequency waveform inversion: reading system inertia and generation mix off the 1-second trace
all_candidates.one_line: Invert the power system's micro-dynamics - infer how much rotating inertia and which generation technologies are online from the frequency waveform alone.
all_candidates.output_label: Instantaneous system inertia (GVA-s), online synchronous capacity by technology class, and governor/damping response parameters; secondarily, loss-of-infeed event detection and size.

all_candidates.g1_corpus: NREL PVDAQ public datasets on OEDI (https://data.openei.org/submissions/4568), DKASC Alice Springs, the ANU 'Quality Controlled Power Output Time Series Data from 1287 Solar PV Systems in Australia' (https://datacommons.anu.edu.au/DataCommons/rest/display/anudc:5953), and PVOutput.org public systems with declared metadata; pvlib-python as the free forward model.
all_candidates.g1_est_units: UNVERIFIED at the system level - I could not confirm public system counts for PVDAQ or PVOutput and will not guess; verified anchors are 1,287 systems (ANU). Counting units as system-days, 1e4 systems x several years exceeds 1e6, but the count of INDEPENDENT systems is the honest bottleneck and is probably 1e3-1e5.
all_candidates.g2_mechanism: (a/c) Two-stage: declared system metadata (tilt, azimuth, kW) on real public systems forms the small labelled seed, exactly like the 40k contractor hours; pvlib then forward-simulates unlimited (parameter vector -> power series) pairs under real historical irradiance (NSRDB, free), and the inverse model trained on the union is applied to the unlabelled long tail of metered sites.
all_candidates.g3_argument: Behind-the-meter DER invisibility is a worsening operational problem, and the inverse is genuinely underdetermined from one day but well-determined from a year - so more data per site and more sites both help. A frontier text model cannot consume 35,000 five-minute power readings.
all_candidates.g3_risk: Strongest attack: this is a well-posed physics fit, and open tools already do it - pvlib plus least squares, NREL's Solar-Data-Tools / PVInsight system profiler. A frontier model with a code interpreter writes the fit in twenty lines and gets a defensible answer, and unlike a learned model it generalises to any array geometry. The learned version has to beat a correct physical model, which is a bad bet.
all_candidates.g5_buyer: Solar asset managers and O&M analytics vendors (Raptor Maps, AlsoEnergy) doing fleet-wide underperformance triage, plus utilities and ISOs needing behind-the-meter DER visibility for load forecasting, and insurers underwriting PV production guarantees.
all_candidates.g6_note: CPU-fine: series are small; pvlib simulation is cheap and parallel. Storage for 1e6 system-days of 5-minute data is a few GB if stored as float32 arrays.
all_candidates.input_modality: Numeric power/energy time series at 5-15 minute cadence plus location and irradiance covariates. Telemetry vectors.
all_candidates.name: PV system parameter inversion from AC power time series
all_candidates.one_line: Recover a solar array's physical configuration - capacity, tilt, azimuth, clipping, shading, soiling and degradation - from its power output alone, for grid operators who cannot see behind the meter.
all_candidates.output_label: DC capacity, tilt, azimuth, DC/AC ratio and clipping onset, module technology class, shading profile by solar position, soiling loss and annual degradation rate.

all_candidates.g1_corpus: FlowRepository (http://flowrepository.org), ImmPort and Cytobank public FCS deposits. Verified scale anchor: 'Robust FCS Parsing: Exploring 211,359 Public Files', Cytometry Part A 2020 https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/cyto.a.24187 - 211,359 public FCS files parsed. CROWDING CHECK: the state of the art is AutoSpill (Nat. Commun. 2021, robust linear regression, shipped in FlowJo) and classical spectral unmixing; I found no learned/at-scale model.
all_candidates.g1_est_units: 2.11e5 public FCS files (verified); at 1e5-1e6 events per file the event-level corpus is 1e10+ vectors. If the unit is the FILE, this is ~2e5 and short of 1e6 - so define the unit as an (event-block, panel) sample to clear G1 honestly.
all_candidates.g2_mechanism: Every observed event is a known linear operator applied to an unobserved abundance vector, and the operator is re-appliable: take compensated/single-stain data, sample physically plausible spillover matrices, and re-mix to manufacture unlimited (mixed event cloud -> true matrix) pairs at zero cost. Real single-stain control tubes already sitting in the repositories give exact anchors for the real-data half.
all_candidates.g3_argument: The valuable version is the blind one - estimating the operator from an experimental tube with no controls - which is a genuine blind-source-separation problem where breadth of panels, fluorophores and instruments is the lever. Input is a numeric point cloud; there is no prompt for it, and no frontier model will ever be trained on raw FCS events because they are not on the open web as text.
all_candidates.g3_risk: Strongest attack: the problem may be one nobody is allowed to have - lab protocol and regulatory guidance mandate single-stain controls, and AutoSpill already solves the controlled case well enough that FlowJo ships it. Blind unmixing is identifiable only up to scaling and permutation without anchors, so the learned model may be structurally unable to beat a two-tube protocol change. Also a frontier model with a code interpreter can run AutoSpill.
all_candidates.g5_buyer: Cytometer manufacturers (BD Biosciences, Cytek, Beckman Coulter) shipping automated panel QC, and clinical flow labs / CROs needing instrument-to-instrument calibration transfer for multi-site trials.
all_candidates.g6_note: Excellent CPU fit: subsample 1e3-1e4 events per file into fixed-size sets; each unit is a few tens of KB. Set-transformer or DeepSets over d<=64 numeric channels trains in minutes-to-hours per scale on 4 cores.
all_candidates.input_modality: Raw FCS event matrices: n x d numeric vectors, d = 10-50 detector channels (up to 64 on spectral instruments), 1e5-1e6 events per file. Unordered numeric point clouds.
all_candidates.name: Blind spectral unmixing: recovering the spillover operator from raw cytometry event clouds
all_candidates.one_line: Estimate a flow cytometer's spillover/unmixing matrix and per-detector calibration directly from an unlabelled experimental file, without the single-stain control tubes the current method requires.
all_candidates.output_label: The d x d spillover/spectral-unmixing matrix, the autofluorescence axis, and per-detector gain/MESF calibration - i.e. the instrument's forward mixing operator.

all_candidates.g1_corpus: PRIDE Archive (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/pride/) - verified 285 petabytes as of August 2024, ~534 new datasets per month, tens of thousands of public datasets ('The PRIDE database at 20 years: 2025 update', NAR 2025 https://academic.oup.com/nar/article/53/D1/D543/7874848); plus MassIVE and MetaboLights. Every dataset ships open-format mzML with full instrument headers, and most ship search results.
all_candidates.g1_est_units: >=1e9 public MS/MS spectra; raw-run count is UNVERIFIED but is at minimum 1e5-1e6 given tens of thousands of datasets with hundreds to thousands of files each (the largest single submission had 7,444 raw files).
all_candidates.g2_mechanism: A search engine is the free oracle. Run Comet or MSFragger once over a file: every confidently identified peptide has an exactly-known theoretical m/z, so the observed-minus-theoretical residual is a measured, dense, free label at thousands of points per run - the instrument's own error field, handed over at CPU cost. Method descriptors come free from the mzML header. Then hide both and learn the inverse from raw peaks alone.
all_candidates.g3_argument: Mass calibration drift is instrument physics - space charge, temperature, vacuum, detector ageing - and is non-analytic per instrument. A model that has seen many instruments, many labs and many chromatographic regimes should predict drift a single-run calibration cannot. The input is a sparse numeric array with 5-decimal m/z values; text tokenisation of high-resolution m/z is a known failure mode, so plain prompting is not merely weak, it is ill-typed.
all_candidates.g3_risk: Strongest attack: two serious efforts already exist - mzRefinery and mzRecal recalibrate from identified peptides, and MassShiftNet is a self-supervised neural mass-recalibration framework - so G4 white space is thin. Modern instruments also carry hardware lock-mass, keeping drift at 1-2 ppm where the remaining headroom may not be worth anything. And if you are going to run a search engine to make labels, the customer can run one too.
all_candidates.g5_buyer: MS instrument vendors (Thermo Fisher, Bruker, Agilent) shipping autonomous calibration and predictive service, and clinical/regulated MS labs that need CLIA- or GxP-grade instrument QC evidence without spiking standards into every run.
all_candidates.g6_note: CPU-feasible on peak lists only. Raw PRIDE is petabyte-scale, so you must stream-subsample: pick a few hundred runs, centroid to peak lists, and store fixed-size top-k peak sets (a few KB per spectrum). 1e6 spectra of top-200 peaks is ~2-4 GB - fits the 30 GB budget.
all_candidates.input_modality: Sparse numeric peak lists: (m/z, intensity, retention time, ion mobility) tuples, thousands per spectrum, comment- and metadata-free. Numeric fields, not text.
all_candidates.name: LC-MS instrument-state inversion: mass-error field and acquisition method from raw peak lists
all_candidates.one_line: Read the physical state of a mass spectrometer off its raw output - reconstruct the run's ppm mass-error surface and the acquisition method that produced it, with no calibrants and no database search.
all_candidates.output_label: The run's mass-error surface (ppm as a function of m/z, RT and ion current), plus acquisition-method descriptors: instrument class, collision energy, LC gradient shape, column chemistry, isolation width.

all_candidates.g1_corpus: Crystallography Open Database, verified 534,680 entries (https://www.crystallography.net/cod/, checked 2026-08); Materials Project; RRUFF for experimental mineral patterns; pymatgen and GSAS-II as free forward simulators. CROWDING CHECK, AND IT IS BAD: SimXRD-4M (ICLR 2025, https://github.com/Bin-Cao/SimXRD) already publishes 4M+ simulated patterns over 119,000 structures under 33 experimental conditions, and a 2019 Nat. Commun. work trained on 1,785,405 synthetic patterns.
all_candidates.g1_est_units: 5.35e5 crystal structures (verified) x sampled conditions => >1e7 simulable patterns. But an open corpus at target scale ALREADY EXISTS (SimXRD-4M, 4e6 patterns), which is precisely what G4 forbids.
all_candidates.g2_mechanism: Every diffraction pattern is a deterministic function of a CIF plus instrument and microstructure parameters. Forward-simulate from COD/MP entries with sampled profile parameters, preferred orientation, background and noise; the sampled parameters are the labels. Zero marginal cost, CPU only.
all_candidates.g3_argument: Scaling in structure diversity and condition diversity plausibly helps, and the input (a 5,000-point intensity vector) is not something a text model consumes. But the honest scaling story here is weaker than the other candidates because the downstream solver (Rietveld least squares) already converges given a decent starting point.
all_candidates.g3_risk: This one fails G4, not G3, and I am flagging it rather than dressing it up: SimXRD-4M is an open 4-million-pattern benchmark published at ICLR 2025, so 'no open dataset at target scale' is false, and multiple deep-learning XRD phase-ID papers exist. On top of that, Rietveld refinement is a mature, well-conditioned optimiser, and the genuinely hard case - unknown phases in a real experimental pattern - is a sim-to-real problem that more simulated data does not fix. Include only if the study is narrowed to instrument-profile inversion on REAL experimental patterns, where I did not find prior work.
all_candidates.g5_buyer: Pharmaceutical solid-form and QC laboratories doing polymorph quantification under GMP, and diffractometer vendors (Bruker AXS, Malvern Panalytical) selling automated quantitative phase analysis.
all_candidates.g6_note: Very CPU-friendly: patterns are 2-10k floats, 1e6 patterns is ~20-40 GB at float32 and ~10-20 GB at float16 or downsampled - fits with care. 1D CNN trains fast on 4 cores.
all_candidates.input_modality: 1D intensity-vs-2theta vectors, 2,000-10,000 points, plus wavelength. Numeric spectra.
all_candidates.name: Rietveld pre-solve: instrument-profile and microstructure inversion from powder diffraction
all_candidates.one_line: Turn a raw 1D powder pattern into a converged Rietveld starting model - instrument profile, lattice, phase fractions and microstructure - instead of just classifying its space group.
all_candidates.output_label: Caglioti profile terms (U, V, W), zero-shift and asymmetry, lattice parameters, weight fractions for each phase in a mixture, and crystallite size / microstrain.

all_candidates.g1_corpus: Kansas Geological Survey Magellan LAS archive (https://www.kgs.ku.edu/Magellan/Logs/) - verified 21,780 LAS-format digital wireline logs as of 2024-12-31; the KGS Walters Digital Geological Library holds 2,984,789 digital well logs and documents (mostly rasters). Sodir/NPD DISKOS (Norway), USGS, Utah FORGE and several US state surveys publish additional open LAS.
all_candidates.g1_est_units: ~2.2e4 open LAS wells in Kansas alone (verified); pooling state surveys and NPD plausibly reaches 1e5 wells. As depth samples: ~1e8. If the unit is a 100-ft log interval, >1e6 units is comfortably clear - but the count of INDEPENDENT wells is ~1e5, which is the honest limit.
all_candidates.g2_mechanism: (b) The LAS header already records service company, tool mnemonics, run date, mud properties and hole size - free metadata labels sitting unused on top of the numeric curves, for every file. (c) Published tool-response models and borehole-correction charts can forward-simulate a given formation's response under sampled borehole conditions, generating unlimited (corrected -> raw) pairs.
all_candidates.g3_argument: Cross-vendor, cross-vintage inconsistency is the standing obstacle to basin-scale subsurface models, and it is a per-instrument inverse that gets better with more wells and more tool types. The input is a numeric depth series; no prompting formulation exists.
all_candidates.g3_risk: Strongest attack: much of the label is literally in the file header, so the 'recovery' task is unnecessary wherever the header survives; and curve reconstruction specifically is crowded - it has been the subject of SPWLA/SPE/FORCE-2020 ML contests for years, with public leaderboards. Petrophysicists also have deterministic chart-book corrections that are defensible to a regulator in a way a neural net is not.
all_candidates.g5_buyer: Carbon-storage developers and geothermal operators (and the state geological surveys serving them) doing basin-scale screening across decades of heterogeneous legacy logs, where inconsistent vintages currently force manual normalisation.
all_candidates.g6_note: CPU-fine for LAS text curves (a well is ~1-10 MB, so 1e4 wells is tens of GB - subsample intervals). The 2.98M raster logs are IMAGES and would break both G6 and the compute budget; exclude them.
all_candidates.input_modality: Multi-curve numeric depth series (gamma ray, resistivity array, bulk density, neutron porosity, sonic slowness) sampled every 0.5 ft over thousands of feet. Instrument telemetry against depth.
all_candidates.name: Wireline log harmonisation: inverting tool, vendor and borehole-environment effects
all_candidates.one_line: Learn the instrument signature in a well log - which service company's tool string and vintage produced it, what borehole corrections it needs, and what the missing curves would have read.
all_candidates.output_label: Service-company/tool-string/vintage class, borehole-environmental correction terms (mud weight, hole-size, standoff, invasion), and reconstruction of absent curves in a common normalised reference frame.

all_candidates.g1_corpus: Public cycling archives: Severson/Attia MATR (https://data.matr.io), CALCE, NASA PCoE, Battery Archive (batteryarchive.org). VERIFIED SCALE: Severson is 124 commercial LFP cells with ~96,700 total cycles; the combined Severson+Attia MATR set is 169-180 cells and is described in the literature as the LARGEST public full-cycle dataset; CALCE contributes ~13-15 cells.
all_candidates.g1_est_units: G1 FAIL. ~1.8e2 cells in the largest public set, ~1e5 cycles total across the major archives - two to four orders of magnitude short of 1e6 independent units. Simulated PyBaMM data is unlimited but is manufactured, not an existing abundant corpus, so it cannot rescue G1 on its own terms.
all_candidates.g2_mechanism: PyBaMM/DFN is a free simulator: sample parameter vectors, integrate, emit voltage curves - exact labels at CPU cost. The label manufacturer is genuinely excellent; the problem is that there is almost no real unlabelled corpus for it to label.
all_candidates.g3_argument: Would have been strong - the inverse is ill-posed from a single cycle and well-posed from a lifetime, so more cells and more compute help, and voltage traces are not in web-text distribution.
all_candidates.g3_risk: Beyond the G1 failure: BatteryML already exists as an open ML-on-battery-degradation platform, and parameter identification via PyBaMM plus optimisation is standard practice. A purely simulation-trained model faces a sim-to-real gap with only ~180 real cells to validate against, so the scaling curve is unverifiable - which is exactly the failure mode that kills a funding thesis.
all_candidates.g5_buyer: Battery manufacturers and EV OEM warranty/state-of-health teams, plus second-life and grid-storage operators - but the data they would need is behind NDA, which is the reason G1 fails.
all_candidates.g6_note: CPU-feasible in principle (cycles are small arrays, PyBaMM runs on CPU), but you cannot build 4 data scales spanning 2 orders of magnitude from real data - only from simulation, which makes the scaling study self-referential. Do not pick this one.
all_candidates.input_modality: Numeric voltage/current/temperature traces per charge-discharge cycle, plus derived dQ/dV curves. Compact telemetry.
all_candidates.name: Battery electrochemical parameter inversion from cycling curves (G1 FAIL - recorded for completeness)
all_candidates.one_line: Recover a lithium-ion cell's internal electrochemical parameters and degradation modes from its terminal voltage/current traces - attractive on every gate except the one that matters first.
all_candidates.output_label: Physics-based model parameters (electrode stoichiometry limits, diffusivities, film resistance) and degradation-mode attribution (LLI, LAM-pe, LAM-ne).

all_candidates.g1_corpus: Point sources: OpenStreetMap node coordinates (ODbL, planet dumps, https://planet.openstreetmap.org), USGS GNIS, Natural Earth, GADM. CRS definitions: EPSG Geodetic Parameter Dataset (https://epsg.org) as shipped in PROJ's proj.db (https://proj.org). Real unlabelled target corpus: orphan shapefiles/CSVs with missing or broken .prj on data.gov, state/EU open-data portals, and archived GIS holdings.
all_candidates.g1_est_units: CRS definitions in EPSG/proj.db: UNVERIFIED (order 10^3-10^4). OSM planet node count: UNVERIFIED here (order 10^9-10^10, publicly documented). Labelled pairs are effectively unbounded because every (point-set x CRS) pairing is a free sample; >=10^6 units is trivially reachable. Size of the real orphan-.prj corpus: UNVERIFIED.
all_candidates.g2_mechanism: PROJ/GDAL is the label manufacturer and it is free, deterministic and exact. Take any geographic point set, push it through any CRS in proj.db, and you have an exactly-labelled (coordinates -> EPSG + parameters) sample at ~microsecond cost. Add realistic corruption operators (axis swap, truncation to 2 decimals, unit confusion feet/metres, wrong datum, coordinate order flip, clipped extents, small point counts) to match the real orphan-file distribution. No human annotation anywhere in the loop.
all_candidates.g3_argument: Input is a list of numbers; there is no prompt a language model can write that expresses 'regress the central meridian of this point cloud'. More CRSs, more geographies, more corruption operators, and more points per sample all monotonically increase the amount of signal, and the task has genuine long-tail structure (national grids, historical datums, oil-industry local grids) that only shows up at scale. Bigger general models do not help because the modality is wrong.
all_candidates.g3_risk: The strongest attack is NOT an LLM, it is exhaustive search: enumerate all ~10^3-10^4 CRSs in proj.db, inverse-project the points, and score each hypothesis against a coastline/landmass raster or a country-boundary polygon. That brute-force baseline is cheap, interpretable, and probably beats a small learned model on the easy 90% of cases; commercial 'Projection Finder' and QGIS heuristics already do a coarse version. The thesis only survives if the learned model wins on the hard residue (custom/local grids not in EPSG, points in featureless ocean or a single city block, datum-only ambiguity where two CRSs differ by metres). That residue must be shown to be a real and large fraction, or the domain dies here. Secondary risk: a frontier model with a code interpreter can WRITE the brute-force search, which is functionally 'plain prompting eats it' at the system level.
all_candidates.g5_buyer: Geospatial data-integration vendors (Safe Software/FME, Esri, Bentley) and national mapping/archival agencies who must ingest decades of orphaned vector files whose projection metadata is lost.
all_candidates.g6_note: Units are a few hundred float pairs each; 10^6 units fits in ~1-3 GB. Label generation is pure CPU via pyproj. Four scales 10^3/10^4/10^5/10^6 trivially trainable on 4 cores with a small transformer or set-encoder (DeepSets/PointNet-style) in hours.
all_candidates.input_modality: Arrays of raw numeric coordinate pairs (float64), plus optional neighbour-topology features. No text, no imagery. Explicitly NOT in web-text pretraining distribution.
all_candidates.name: CRS-Recover: projection/datum identification from bare coordinate arrays
all_candidates.one_line: Given only an array of numeric (x,y[,z]) pairs with no .prj/metadata, recover the EPSG coordinate reference system and datum-shift parameters that produced them.
all_candidates.output_label: EPSG code (extreme multi-class over the PROJ/EPSG registry) + regression head on projection parameters (central meridian, false easting/northing, scale factor) + datum/epoch.

all_candidates.g1_corpus: Google Fonts (OFL, https://github.com/google/fonts), Noto (210 families, ~64,000 characters covered), Font Squirrel / Open Font Library, GitHub `opentype-fonts` topic, and every system font. Each font file carries its own free labels in the `cmap` table. Real unlabelled target corpus: subset/embedded fonts inside PDFs in Internet Archive, CORE, and government e-filing archives that ship no ToUnicode CMap.
all_candidates.g1_est_units: SVG-Fonts (SVG-VAE lineage) is VERIFIED at 14 million glyph examples drawn from ~220,000 fonts - but restricted to 62 Latin alphanumerics. Noto alone covers ~64,000 characters across 210 families (verified). Total glyph instances across open font archives: UNVERIFIED, but >=10^7 is well supported by the 220k-font figure alone.
all_candidates.g2_mechanism: The outline is the artifact; the structured source that generated the pairing (the font's `cmap` table mapping codepoint -> glyph ID -> charstring) is still present in every font file. fontTools extracts (outline, codepoint) pairs at near-zero cost with zero human labelling. Augment with the real-world corruption process: subsetting, glyph-ID renumbering, custom/PUA re-encoding, and Type 3 conversion - exactly what PDF producers do when they destroy the mapping.
all_candidates.g3_argument: The moat is not 'recognise the letter A'. It is the tail: private-use-area re-encodings, symbol/math/dingbat/musical fonts, Indic conjunct glyphs, CJK, and heavily subsetted fonts where the same shape is legitimately ambiguous and context is required. More fonts and more scripts strictly increase coverage of that tail, and the task is a pure recognition problem where scale is known to help.
all_candidates.g3_risk: Brutal version: rasterise the outline to a 64x64 bitmap, hand it to any frontier vision model, and it reads the character - for Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, CJK and most Indic, that works today with plain prompting and no training at all. It is one `draw()` call away. So the whole thesis reduces to the residue where there is no visual answer (PUA, corporate icon fonts, ligature glyphs with no single codepoint, homoglyph disambiguation) - and that residue may be small. Second, G4 is partly compromised: SVG-Fonts already exists as an open 14M-example vector-glyph dataset (though Latin-62 only), and vector-font transformers (arXiv 2502.00250 font classification, DeepVecFont, VecFontSDF, VecGlypher) mean vector-glyph modelling is not white space; only the codepoint-recovery framing and the full-Unicode scale are.
all_candidates.g5_buyer: PDF text-extraction and e-discovery vendors (Adobe, Foxit, Datalogics, iText, Relativity) and national digital libraries whose Indic/CJK/legacy PDF holdings currently return garbage on copy-paste.
all_candidates.g6_note: A glyph is typically <300 outline points; 10^6 glyphs at int16 fits in well under 1 GB. fontTools extraction is pure CPU. Four scales from 10^3 to 10^6 glyphs are comfortable on 4 cores with a small sequence model. No rasterisation needed (and deliberately avoided - rasterising is what hands the task to a VLM).
all_candidates.input_modality: Bezier/quadratic contour command sequences (moveTo/lineTo/curveTo + int16 coordinates in font units) plus advance width and side bearings. Vector command streams, not pixels and not text.
all_candidates.name: GlyphMap: Unicode codepoint recovery from vector glyph outlines
all_candidates.one_line: Given only a glyph's Bezier outline (no rasterisation, no cmap), predict the Unicode codepoint it encodes - the missing-ToUnicode problem that makes millions of archived PDFs uncopyable.
all_candidates.output_label: Unicode codepoint (extreme multi-class over ~10^5 codepoints) plus auxiliary heads: script, general category, and 'is genuinely non-textual/PUA symbol'.

all_candidates.g1_corpus: PDMX (VERIFIED: >250,000 public-domain MusicXML scores scraped from MuseScore, released as an open dataset), MuseScore.com (VERIFIED: >1.5 million score files downloadable in MuseScore/MusicXML/MIDI), IMSLP (VERIFIED: >210,000 works), KernScores/Humdrum, OpenScore Lieder (>1,300 songs) and the OpenScore Orchestral corpus. Engravers: LilyPond (GPL) and Verovio (LGPL), both open and scriptable.
all_candidates.g1_est_units: Scores: 250,000 verified public-domain MusicXML (PDMX) up to ~1.5M on MuseScore.com. Layout DECISIONS per score is the real unit: hundreds to thousands per score, so >=10^7-10^8 decision units from PDMX alone. Exact decisions-per-score figure: UNVERIFIED.
all_candidates.g2_mechanism: Run LilyPond/Verovio over the score corpus and dump the engraver's internal grob (graphical object) tree - every break, spring, beam slope and slur control point with exact coordinates. The engraved artifact is generated from the structured source (MusicXML/MEI) which still exists, and the generator is public, so both sides of every pair are free. Cost per score is a sub-second CPU render. A second, higher-value label source is shape (a): use the model as an inverse engraver against scanned historic engravings (Peters, Breitkopf plates on IMSLP) to pseudo-label human house-style decisions.
all_candidates.g3_argument: The output is continuous geometry in staff spaces, produced by a global optimisation over a whole system/page. A language model cannot emit 'beam slope = 0.37 staff spaces over 4 notes' from a prompt; it has never seen that number space. Scaling helps because engraving conventions are a huge, sparse, style-conditional rule set (Gould/Ross conventions plus publisher house styles) that only becomes learnable with many scores and many publishers.
all_candidates.g3_risk: The strongest attack is trivial and near-fatal: if you want a layout, RUN THE ENGRAVER. LilyPond and Verovio are free, deterministic and already better than any small model will be; a frontier model with a shell can just invoke them. So a model that merely imitates LilyPond has zero economic reason to exist. The thesis only survives if the target is a layout the engraver CANNOT produce - a specific publisher's house style learned from scanned plates, or real-time incremental relayout inside an editor where a full engraver pass is too slow. That reframing shifts the ground truth from free (shape c) to scarce (shape a on scanned plates), which weakens G1/G2. Also note this sits close to OMR, a crowded field, and the same corpora (KernScores+Verovio, GrandStaff) are already used there for rendering, so reviewers will confuse the two.
all_candidates.g5_buyer: Notation-software vendors (Steinberg Dorico, Avid Sibelius, MuseScore, Newzik) and music publishers (Hal Leonard, Boosey & Hawkes, Peters) who pay human engravers to fix automatic layout.
all_candidates.g6_note: Both the render (label manufacture) and the model are CPU work. A decision unit is a short typed sequence plus a handful of floats; 10^6 decisions fit in a few hundred MB. LilyPond rendering of 10^5 scores on 4 cores is the slow part (hours to a couple of days) - Verovio is much faster and is the right choice for the large scales.
all_candidates.input_modality: Structured symbolic music graph: event onsets/durations in rational time, pitch lattice, voice/staff assignment, articulation flags. A typed graph of numeric fields, not prose and not an image.
all_candidates.name: Engraver: music engraving layout-decision prediction from symbolic score
all_candidates.one_line: Given the semantic content of a score (notes, rests, voices, dynamics) predict the engraver's layout decisions - system/page breaks, horizontal spacing, beam slopes, slur control points, collision offsets - as continuous geometry.
all_candidates.output_label: Layout geometry: break positions (sequence labelling), x-offsets in staff spaces (regression), beam start/end y in staff spaces, slur/tie Bezier control points, accidental and dot displacement vectors, page-turn placement.

all_candidates.g1_corpus: Synthesis side: any public structured dataset (US Census public-use files, IRS SOI, CMS Medicare public-use files, NARA electronic records, Bureau of Labor Statistics fixed-width extracts) serialised to fixed-width/EBCDIC via open serialisers (Cobrix, cobol-copybook.jsonifier, GnuCOBOL). Real side: NARA's electronic-records holdings and government fixed-width public-use files that still ship a data dictionary, plus the very large private inventories that motivated US patents 9372881 and 8756258 ('tens to hundreds of thousands of VSAM or sequential data files' with no metadata catalogue - VERIFIED patent language).
all_candidates.g1_est_units: Records are the unit and they are effectively unbounded: one public-use microdata file yields 10^6-10^8 records, and every (dataset x random layout x codepage x packing choice) is a fresh labelled sample. Count of real orphaned legacy files in public archives: UNVERIFIED.
all_candidates.g2_mechanism: Shape (b): a COBOL serialiser is a deterministic environment that supplies exact ground truth - generate a random copybook (field order, PIC clauses, COMP-3/COMP/DISPLAY, signs, OCCURS DEPENDING ON), serialise real tabular data through it, and you get byte streams with exact field boundaries at zero marginal cost. Shape (c): government fixed-width public-use files were generated from a documented layout that is still published, so real (bytes, layout) pairs exist for free to calibrate the synthetic distribution and to measure sim-to-real gap.
all_candidates.g3_argument: The signal lives in byte-level statistics - nibble distributions of packed decimal, sign nibbles C/D/F, EBCDIC digit runs 0xF0-0xF9, alignment periodicity, high-order-byte entropy of binary integers. A frontier general model reasoning over a hex dump degrades fast beyond a few hundred bytes, and cannot integrate evidence across 10^5 records of the same file, which is exactly where the structure becomes identifiable. More records per file and more layout diversity monotonically sharpen the segmentation posterior.
all_candidates.g3_risk: Honest strongest case: a frontier model given a 2 KB hex dump plus a code tool will write a script that computes column-wise byte entropy and nibble histograms, and will correctly call 'offset 40-45 is COMP-3' on the easy majority. Classical unsupervised segmentation (periodicity + entropy + change-point detection) is also strong and needs no training. The genuinely hard cases - REDEFINES driven by a discriminator field, OCCURS DEPENDING ON, mixed record types in one file, packed fields with no separator - are exactly where labelled synthetic data helps, but they may be a minority of real files. Second risk: sim-to-real. If synthetic copybooks do not match the weird conventions of 1970s insurance and banking layouts, the scaling curve on synthetic data is meaningless. That must be measured on the real government fixed-width files before anything else.
all_candidates.g5_buyer: Mainframe-modernisation and data-migration vendors (IBM, OpenText/Micro Focus, Modern Systems, Astadia) plus national archives (NARA and equivalents) sitting on legacy sequential data whose layout documentation is lost.
all_candidates.g6_note: Records are 80-4000 bytes; 10^6 records is at most ~2-4 GB and can be trimmed to fit. A byte-level 1D conv or small transformer over 512-byte windows trains on CPU. Label manufacture is a pure-Python serialiser. Four scales 10^3->10^6 records are easy.
all_candidates.input_modality: Raw byte streams, typically EBCDIC (CP037/CP1047) fixed-length records of 80-4000 bytes. Byte-level, explicitly outside web-text pretraining distribution.
all_candidates.name: CopybookLM: record-layout induction from undocumented fixed-width and EBCDIC byte streams
all_candidates.one_line: Given a raw legacy data file whose COBOL copybook / record layout is lost, recover the field boundaries, types (COMP-3 packed decimal, zoned, binary, EBCDIC text), record length, and REDEFINES/OCCURS structure from bytes alone.
all_candidates.output_label: Per-byte-offset field segmentation + per-field type tag + record-length hypothesis + variable-layout (REDEFINES/occurs-depending-on) discriminator field identification.

all_candidates.g1_corpus: OpenSky Network historical ADS-B (VERIFIED: >30 trillion ADS-B/Mode S/TCAS/FLARM messages from >5000 sensors, with a >40 trillion Mode S reply figure more recently; research access free, and Impala/Trino history plus published derived datasets). FAA Coded Instrument Flight Procedures (CIFP) in ARINC 424 v18 is a VERIFIED free public download, updated every 28 days (faa.gov/air_traffic/flight_info/aeronav/digital_products/cifp). Eurocontrol/EAD and open AIXM sources extend coverage. Open-source parsers exist (github.com/rstory1/parseCifp).
all_candidates.g1_est_units: ADS-B messages: >30 trillion (verified). Distinct flights extractable: UNVERIFIED but OpenSky-derived public flight tables are in the 10^8 range. Number of procedures in a CIFP cycle: UNVERIFIED (order 10^4 for the US). >=10^6 flight trajectories is comfortably reachable.
all_candidates.g2_mechanism: Shape (c): CIFP is the structured source that generated every published procedure chart and every FMS database - the exact geometric definition of each leg is free and machine-readable, so geometric matching of a trajectory against CIFP produces a labelled seed at zero cost for the clean, on-procedure flights. Shape (a): train an inverse model on that clean seed (plus simulator-generated trajectories from BlueSky/X-Plane flying coded procedures under randomised wind and aircraft type), then pseudo-label the vastly larger corpus of messy real trajectories - vectored arrivals, partial procedures, missed approaches - that the geometric matcher rejects. That is precisely the VPT structure: a small exactly-labelled seed bootstrapping a huge unlabelled corpus.
all_candidates.g3_argument: The input is a numeric flight path; there is no natural-language expression of the task. The value is entirely in the messy tail the deterministic matcher cannot handle, which is where the pseudo-labelling loop earns its keep, and that tail grows with corpus size. More flights, more airports, more weather conditions and more aircraft types all improve coverage of procedure variants.
all_candidates.g3_risk: Strongest attack: this is a geometric matching problem and a well-tuned DTW/Frechet matcher against CIFP with a Viterbi decode over leg types is a strong, explainable, training-free baseline - and it is roughly what airspace-analytics vendors already ship. So the ML thesis has to win specifically on flights that were vectored off procedure, flown with FMS discontinuities, or at airports where the CIFP cycle in force differs from the one you downloaded (procedures change every 28 days, so historical alignment is a data-engineering trap that could dominate the error budget). A frontier model with a code tool can write the matcher. Also, ADS-B ML is not virgin territory - trajectory prediction, anomaly detection and Classi-Fly-style inference papers exist - though procedure/leg recovery specifically appears unoccupied.
all_candidates.g5_buyer: Airspace-analytics and flight-ops vendors (Flightradar24/FlightAware, Jeppesen/Boeing Digital, ForeFlight) and airports/ANSPs who must prove noise-abatement and RNAV-procedure conformance to regulators.
