searches.query: Ghidra IDA Pro automatic base address detection plugin unknown architecture reverseengineering discussion
searches.result_summary: Confirms the problem is live and UNSOLVED in practice. Open issue e-m-b-a/embark#174 'Automatically guessing the base address of a firmware image' (https://github.com/e-m-b-a/embark/issues/174) proposes bolting existing guess-scripts on and surfacing a list of candidate bases — i.e. the state of the art shipped to analysts is still 'here are N guesses'. Pen Test Partners 'Taming the dragon: RE firmware with Ghidra' and SVD-Loader (ARM CMSIS-SVD) confirm analysts still supply the base by hand or from a datasheet.

searches.query: LLM large language model recover firmware load address memory map raw blob 2026
searches.result_summary: All LLM firmware work is strictly DOWNSTREAM of loading — it consumes Ghidra pseudo-code, never raw bytes: FIRMHIVE / 'LLMs as Firmware Experts: A Runtime-Grown Tree-of-Agents' (arXiv 2511.18438), 'Securing LLM-Generated Embedded Firmware' (arXiv 2509.09970), ONEKEY blog, Saptang Labs 'How LLMs Automate Ghidra Firmware Analysis'. No LLM takes a headerless blob and emits a base address. Also AgentRE-Bench v3 evaluates frontier models on Windows PE binaries via static-analysis TOOLS, not raw bytes.

searches.query: Assemblage dataset binaries corpus scale million PE ELF labeled ground truth
searches.result_summary: Corpus claim verified. Assemblage (arXiv 2405.03991, https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.03991) = 890k Windows PE + 428k Linux ELF across 29 build configurations, with PDB/DWARF ground truth; datasheet at https://assemblage-dataset.net/assets/total-datasheet.pdf. Also Assemblage-DeepHistory (arXiv 2605.21615, 2026): 73,610 binaries, ~442M functions. Note: these are shipped WITH headers and are labelled for function boundaries/names — no one has defined a headerless load-layout task or benchmark over them. paperswithcode.com is now dead (302-redirects to huggingface.co/papers/trending); the ISAdetect dataset page existed there.
searches.venue: Papers With Code / arXiv (corpus check for G1)

serious_efforts.name: ELISA — ELiciting ISA of Raw Binaries for Fine-Grained Code and Data Separation (Pogliani et al.)
serious_efforts.scale: Small: a few thousand binaries scraped from Debian across ~20 architectures; no released corpus at scale, no base-address labels.
serious_efforts.what_it_did: The closest prior art to the full proposal. Takes a raw headerless binary, identifies the ISA with a logistic-regression model over byte/opcode features, then uses supervised sequential learning (CRF) to locate code-section boundaries and predict instruction boundaries inside them. Covers 2 of the 4 proposed labels (ISA + code/data segmentation) but NOT base address and NOT entry point.

serious_efforts.name: ISAdetect (Kairajärvi, Costin, Hämäläinen) — CODASPY 2020
serious_efforts.scale: 98,500 Debian-scraped binaries across 23 architectures, ~27 GB full binaries / ~15 GB code-sections-only. ~10^5 units — one order of magnitude below the 10^6 target, and labelled with ISA ONLY (no base address, no entry point, no segmentation).
serious_efforts.what_it_did: ML detection of CPU architecture, endianness and word size for arbitrary binary files and bare object-code fragments. Directly occupies the 'ISA + endianness + word size' label. Released BOTH a tool (github.com/kairis/isadetect, 70 stars, still maintained Apr 2026) and an open dataset.

serious_efforts.name: LOADSTAR — 'You Can't Judge a Binary by Its Header: Data-Code Separation for Non-Standard ARM Binaries using Pseudo Labels' (Benkraouda, Diwan, Wang), IEEE S&P 2025
serious_efforts.scale: Very small: 444 32-bit ARM ELF training binaries (20M instructions, from the Clemens dataset); eval on 65 + 201 + 119 PLC binaries. Roughly 10^2-10^3 units, ~4 orders of magnitude below target. Tool promised open-source; no public repo findable as of Aug 2026.
serious_efforts.what_it_did: Structurally the SAME trick as the proposal and at a top-tier security venue: train a code/data classifier on labelled standard binaries (where the header supplies free ground truth), then pseudo-label unlabelled non-standard headerless binaries and iteratively self-train with domain-knowledge rule correction. Read the full PDF: it is code/data separation ONLY — no base address, no ISA prediction, no entry point, 32-bit ARM only.

serious_efforts.name: Andreassen & Morrison — 'Discovery of Endianness and Instruction Size Characteristics in Binary Programs from Unknown ISAs' (arXiv 2410.21558)
serious_efforts.scale: Two architecture datasets; size not stated in the abstract, small by construction. No release of a 10^6-scale corpus.
serious_efforts.what_it_did: ML prediction of endianness (99.4%), fixed-vs-variable instruction width (86.0%) and fixed instruction size (88.0%) for binaries from ISAs never seen in training. Occupies a slice of the ISA/endianness label and specifically targets the long-tail-ISA generalisation the proposal wants to claim. Does not touch base address. Same group also published 'Call graph discovery in binary programs from unknown ISAs' (arXiv 2401.07565).

serious_efforts.name: cpu_rec (Airbus Security Lab) + cpu_rec_rs
serious_efforts.scale: 72-architecture reference corpus, small (tens of MB); no labelled dataset released for training others.
serious_efforts.what_it_did: The de-facto production answer to 'what ISA is this blob'. Markov-chain / cross-entropy statistical classifier over 72 architectures, shipped as a binwalk plugin; also detects the ISA of a SUB-REGION of a file, which is a weak form of code/data-region segmentation. 752 GitHub stars, last updated Aug 2026. Not a trained deep model, but it is the incumbent that any learned ISA classifier must beat.

serious_efforts.name: Large Byte Model — 'Teaching Language Models About Compiled Code' (Störtz, Stan, Dinu, Servia-Rodríguez, Gaman, Miron, Raff)
serious_efforts.scale: Not disclosed in the abstract; the companion Binary BPE work (arXiv 2511.17573) trains on ~10 GB of raw binary. No checkpoint or dataset release stated.
serious_efforts.what_it_did: Byte-tokenizer + vocabulary-expansion LM over RAW EXECUTABLE BYTES — i.e. the exact modality moat the proposal relies on is already being claimed. Reports 98% architecture classification and 69% malware-family classification. Deployed to analysts. Does not do base address, entry point, or code/data segmentation, and does not target headerless firmware.

serious_efforts.name: The heuristic base-address literature + tool ecosystem (binbloom v2, rbasefind, basefind2, allyourbase; FIND-LP / FIND-String / FIND-LDR / MIPS absolute-address statistics / function-address matching)
serious_efforts.scale: Each paper evaluates on tens of firmware images. No released dataset, no benchmark, no leaderboard.
serious_efforts.what_it_did: Not ML, but this is the incumbent that owns the base-address task. Five-plus peer-reviewed papers (Digital Investigation 2016, IJCIP 2016, Computers & Security 2019, WCMC 2021) plus four widely used open-source tools all recover the image base by matching string offsets, literal pools, function-pointer arrays or absolute-address histograms against candidate bases. They are deterministic, fast, and already correct on well-formed ARM/MIPS images — which is both the baseline to beat and a G3 hazard.

g4_results.domain: CopybookLM: record-layout induction from undocumented fixed-width and EBCDIC byte streams (per-byte field segmentation + field type tag + record length + REDEFINES/OCCURS discriminator, from bytes alone)
g4_results.g4_reasoning:
Sixteen searches across arXiv (three separate full listings), dblp, GitHub (MCP API), HuggingFace datasets API, Papers-with-Code-adjacent benchmark search, USPTO, and four domain venues — NDSS/CCS/IEEE-ACM ToN (the security community that owns binary field inference), WCRE/ICSME (software reengineering, which owns legacy data reverse engineering), POPL/PADL (data description languages), and the IBM mainframe practitioner forums plus the SourceForge JRecord/RecordEditor tool ecosystem — plus VLDB/SIGMOD and iPRES as negative checks.

IN-DOMAIN EFFORTS: essentially one, and it is a hand-tool. RecordEditor's fixed-width field search / FileWizard is the only artifact anywhere that attempts to find fields in an undocumented fixed-width or mainframe file, and when I fetched its documentation it turned out to be an interactive colour-the-columns wizard where the human clicks each boundary. No model, no benchmark, no number.

THREE INDEPENDENT EMPTINESS SIGNALS, each strong on its own: (1) dblp returns 4 hits for 'copybook' and all four are the HANDWRITING sense — the COBOL sense has never appeared in a dblp-indexed title; dblp returns 3 hits for 'EBCDIC', all from 1971-1973. (2) The complete 34-paper arXiv COBOL corpus, which is booming in 2024-2026, is 100% code-side (translation, LLM codegen, modernization agents, equivalence testing) with literally zero data-side papers — the field has collectively decided COBOL means source code. (3) HuggingFace returns 0 datasets for copybook, ebcdic, record layout, fixed width, and packed-decimal.

ADJACENT CROWDING IS REAL BUT DOES NOT TRANSFER. The protocol-RE line (BinaryInferno NDSS'23, DynPRE NDSS'24, BinPRE CCS'24, DL-ProS² ToN'24) is genuinely active on the same abstract task shape — field boundaries from bytes — and I am counting it as one serious adjacent effort rather than dismissing it. But it takes network traffic (often needing a live endpoint or the client binary), evaluates on ~10 hand-labelled protocols, has no ground-truth generator, and has no concept of the things that define this domain: EBCDIC code pages, COMP-3/zoned/COMP encodings, sign nybbles, record-length hypothesis search, REDEFINES, OCCURS DEPENDING ON. Its released corpora are ~10 protocols, not 10^6 records. Notably, its best reported numbers (0.73 F1) are on structurally easier data, which argues the task is hard rather than done. The two other adjacent lines are worse fits still: Hainaut's database reverse engineering (WCRE'96 through ~2011) recovers structure from COBOL SOURCE and DDL — exactly the artifacts that are missing in the lost-copybook case — and BIEBER (arXiv:2104.09669) needs an instrumented executing parser program.

NO OPEN DATASET AT ANY SCALE. Zero labelled (byte stream, layout) corpora exist on HuggingFace, in the protocol-RE releases, or anywhere else found. Nearest artifact is Binary-30K (30k executables, malware labels, no field layouts) — four orders of magnitude short and the wrong labels.

STRUCTURALLY, the most telling finding is an asymmetry the GitHub search made explicit: the copybook SERIALISER ecosystem is mature and open-source (cobrix at 170 stars, JRecord, cb2xml, legstar, copybook4java, ballerina-copybook, CopybookInputFormat) and every single one consumes a copybook to decode bytes — while 'copybook inference layout' returns total_count 0. The forward direction is a solved, well-engineered, zero-marginal-cost deterministic function; the inverse direction has no repo, no paper, and no dataset. That is exactly the FDM-1 shape: a free label manufacturer sitting unused next to an untouched inverse problem, with the practitioner forums showing the inverse being done by hand from hex dumps today.

Two honest caveats for the parent, neither of which changes the PASS: (a) commercial mainframe-modernization vendors (IBM watsonx Code Assistant for Z, AWS Transform, Blu Age, Precisely, K2view, IBA Group) may have unpublished internal layout-discovery heuristics — the public material I found uniformly requires the copybook, and Gartner's 'AI-assisted reverse engineering' framing surfaced in that search is about CODE, but absence of publication is not proof of absence of product. (b) Semantic Scholar's API rate-limited me (HTTP 429) and arXiv's API did too, so the arXiv coverage came via the HTML search interface rather than the full-text API; the three separate arXiv listings plus dblp make me confident this did not hide anything, but it is a real gap in method.

open_datasets.name: Binary-30K (adjacent only — NOT a record-layout dataset; listed for completeness because it is the nearest thing to a byte-level structured corpus on HuggingFace)
open_datasets.size: 29,793 binaries with byte-level BPE tokenization; labels are malware/benign + platform metadata, NOT field layouts

searches.query: arxiv.org/search all: COBOL (50 results, full listing)
searches.result_summary: 34 results, complete listing retrieved. Every single one is about CODE: COBOL-to-Java/C/Python translation and validation (2607.28271, 2607.04092, 2605.09894, 2508.05199, 2507.23356, 2506.10999, 2504.10548), LLM code generation for COBOL (2604.03986 COBOL-Coder, 2604.03978 COBOLAssist), modernization agents (2605.18684 Reversa, 2605.17535 AgentModernize, 2603.20028 Chiron), XMainframe LLM (2408.04660), X-COBOL dataset of 84 repos / 1,255 COBOL source files (2306.04892), Cobol2Vec (2201.09448), OpenCBS defects (2206.06260). ZERO papers on copybooks, record layouts, EBCDIC, packed decimal, or recovering DATA structure from data files. The entire arXiv COBOL literature is code-side; the data-side is untouched.

searches.query: arxiv.org/search all: copybook OR "packed decimal" OR EBCDIC
searches.result_summary: 2 results total, neither relevant: 'Sub-system self-consistency in coupled cluster theory' (2209.04713, quantum chemistry) and 'Presentation Theorems for Coded Character Sets' (cs/0610168, 2006, group theory applied to character encodings including EBCDIC — about the code page, not record structure). No mainframe data record layout work exists on arXiv.

searches.query: arxiv.org/search all: "file format" inference bytes structure
searches.result_summary: 1 result: BIEBER — 'Inferring Drop-in Binary Parsers from Program Executions' (arXiv:2104.09669, Apr 2021). Regenerates a working parser from INSTRUMENTED PROGRAM EXECUTIONS — it needs the parsing program, which is precisely what is missing in the lost-copybook scenario. Reverse-engineered 6 formats (audio, firmware, bitmap). Adjacent, not competing: dynamic-analysis, not learned-from-bytes, and 6 formats is not a scaling study.

searches.query: arxiv.org/search all: binary format inference field segmentation bytes
searches.result_summary: 1 result: 'Refining Network Message Segmentation with Principal Component Analysis' (arXiv:2301.03585, Nov 2022, Kleber/NEMESYS line). PCA refinement of coarse field boundaries in undocumented NETWORK PROTOCOL messages. Adjacent domain (variable-length wire messages), classical statistics not learned models, no EBCDIC/COMP-3/OCCURS notion.

searches.query: dblp.org/search?q=copybook
searches.result_summary: 4 total matches in all of computer science, and ALL FOUR are the handwriting sense of 'copybook': ICIC 2026 handwriting-recognition corpus from copybooks; RF-Copybook (IMWUT 2017, calligraphy via RFID); 'Generating Copybooks from Consistent Handwriting Styles' (ICDAR 2007); 'Writer Profiling Using Handwriting Copybook Styles' (ICDAR 2005). The COBOL sense of 'copybook' has literally never appeared in a dblp-indexed paper title.

searches.query: dblp.org/search?q=EBCDIC
searches.result_summary: 3 total matches, all from 1971-1973: 'ASCII and EBCDIC Sequencing' (Little, SIGFIDET/SIGMOD Bull. 1973), 'EBCDIC/ASCII Mapping for Network RJE' (RFC 338, 1972), 'EBCDIC Codes and Their Mapping to ASCII' (RFC 183, 1971). Nothing in the last 50 years. This is as empty as a CS subfield gets.

searches.query: binary message format inference protocol reverse engineering NEMESYS BinaryInferno NetPlier field boundaries 2024 2025; plus protocol reverse engineering LLM 2025 2026 survey
searches.result_summary: This is the one genuinely active adjacent line. Found: BinaryInferno (NDSS 2023, https://www.ndss-symposium.org/ndss-paper/binaryinferno-a-semantic-driven-approach-to-field-inference-for-binary-message-formats/) — entropy-based field boundary detection plus float/timestamp detectors, precision 0.69 / recall 0.73; DynPRE (NDSS 2024, https://fouzhe.github.io/publications/paper/NDSS24-DynPRE.pdf) — dynamic inference by probing a live server; BinPRE (CCS 2024, https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3658644.3690299) — binary-analysis-based field inference, 0.73 format perfection / 0.74 F1 semantics, beats BinaryInferno and DynPRE; DL-ProS² 'Crafting Binary Protocol Reversing via Deep Learning With Knowledge-Driven Augmentation' (IEEE/ACM Trans. Networking 2024, https://dl.acm.org/doi/abs/10.1109/TNET.2024.3468350) — U-Net + siamese + BiLSTM-CRF over traffic. IMPORTANT DISTINCTION: all four take NETWORK TRAFFIC (variable-length wire messages, needing a live endpoint or the client binary), all evaluate on ~10 hand-labelled protocols, none has a ground-truth generator, none handles EBCDIC/zoned/COMP-3/COMP/REDEFINES/OCCURS DEPENDING ON, and none trains at scale. Their best F1 ~0.73 on far easier structure shows the task is not solved even next door.
searches.venue: NDSS / ACM CCS / IEEE-ACM ToN (security + networking — domain venue for binary field inference)

searches.query: LearnPADS automatic inference ad hoc data formats Fisher Walker "from dirt to shovels" data description language
searches.result_summary: Found the real foundational work: 'From dirt to shovels: fully automatic tool generation from ad hoc data' (Fisher, Walker, Zhu, White, POPL 2008) and 'LearnPADS++: Incremental Inference of Ad Hoc Data Formats' (PADL 2012, https://tupl.cs.tufts.edu/papers/learnpads-padl2012.pdf), plus the PADS project overview (ICDT 2011, kathleenfisher.org/research/pads/). LearnPADS infers a PADS description from positive examples using MDL/chunking. This is the closest true ancestor — but it is symbolic/MDL, ~15 years old, targets ASCII-ish ad hoc logs (web logs, Netstat, CRT records), assumes tokenizable text, and has no learned model, no scaling curve, and no notion of packed-decimal/zoned/binary-field disambiguation or record-length hypothesis search. Also FlashProfile (arXiv:1709.05725) for syntactic profiles of string columns — text only.
searches.venue: POPL / PADL (programming languages — foundational data-description venue)

searches.query: "data reverse engineering" legacy file structure recovery ICSME SANER WCRE COBOL data structure extraction Hainaut
searches.result_summary: Found the established legacy-data literature: Hainaut et al., 'Structure Elicitation in Database Reverse Engineering' (WCRE 1996), 'Data Structure Extraction in Database Reverse Engineering' (ER workshops 1999, Springer LNCS 1727), 'Database Reverse Engineering' encyclopedia entry (2007), 'Legacy and Future of Data Reverse Engineering' (WCRE 2009), 'Dynamic Program Analysis for Database Reverse Engineering' (GTTSE 2011). Explicitly covers transforming COBOL FILES into relational databases. CRITICAL DIFFERENCE: every one of these recovers structure from the COBOL SOURCE CODE, DDL, program slices, and dynamic program analysis — i.e. from artifacts that exist. None of them attacks the bytes-only case where the code and copybook are both gone. It is symbolic, pre-ML, and the newest entry is 2011-ish.
searches.venue: WCRE / ICSM / ICSME (software reengineering — domain venue for legacy data)

searches.query: GitHub MCP repo search: 'copybook in:name,description,readme' (1,866 hits triaged); 'copybook inference layout'; 'record layout inference binary file'
searches.result_summary: The COBOL half of the 1,866 hits is a healthy ecosystem of copybook CONSUMERS: AbsaOSS/cobrix (170 stars, Spark EBCDIC source), bmTas/JRecord, bmTas/cb2xml, legsem/legstar-core2, NordeaOSS/copybook4java, zalmane/copybook (Python parser), jrperin/cobol-copybook.jsonifier, ballerina-platform/module-ballerinax-copybook, tmalaska/CopybookInputFormat, eclipse-che4z/che-che4z-lsp-for-cobol, aws-samples/aws-mainframe-modernization-carddemo. EVERY ONE requires the copybook as input. 'copybook inference layout' returned total_count 0. 'record layout inference binary file' returned 1 irrelevant hit (an FTC robotics SDK). So: the serialiser infrastructure needed to MANUFACTURE labels is mature and open-source, and the inverse task has zero repos. That asymmetry is the whole thesis.

searches.query: HF datasets API: search=copybook, ebcdic, mainframe, record+layout, fixed+width, packed-decimal
searches.result_summary: copybook: 0. ebcdic: 0. record layout: 0. fixed width: 0. packed-decimal: 0. mainframe: 2, neither relevant — Fsoft-AIC/MainframeBench (209 downloads, COBOL code QA/summarisation) and Tesselexo/Mars-citizen-city-blue-mainframe-siriusABtransmission-data (5 downloads, unrelated). There is NO open dataset of (byte stream, record layout) pairs on HuggingFace at any scale, let alone 10^6.

searches.query: paperswithcode benchmark "structure inference" raw bytes deep learning binary file segmentation dataset
searches.result_summary: No benchmark or leaderboard for record/field layout induction exists. Closest dataset found is Binary-30K (arXiv:2511.22095) — 29,793 executables with byte-level BPE tokenization for malware detection and binary analysis, on HuggingFace. It is labelled with malware/benign and platform metadata, NOT with field layouts, and 30k is four orders of magnitude below the target scale. No leaderboard, no metric, no task definition for the CopybookLM task anywhere.

searches.query: ibmmainframes forum "without copybook" determine layout of a file guess fields packed decimal analyze dump; and COMP-3 packed decimal EBCDIC field detection inference undocumented data file heuristic tool
searches.result_summary: Multiple live threads on exactly this pain: 'To Identify the Packed decimal, Binary value' (ibmmainframes.com/about60718.html), 'Identifying Packed Decimal data in a dataset' (about67490.html), 'Search packed Decimal fields' (about61991.html), 'Unpack COMP/COMP-3 fields' (about62987.html), 'Find Copybook of a dataset used in JCL' (ibmmainframeforum.com t=9891), 'Recovering source code from load module' (about13284.html). The accepted state of the art in practice is a human staring at a hex dump and making informed guesses, byte by byte, and hunting for the copybook in JCL/load modules. Vendor tooling (IBM DataStage, MuleSoft DataWeave copybook format, TextPipe Pro, K2view, Disc Interchange, SimoTime, jatechnologysolutions converters) uniformly REQUIRES the copybook. Confirms an unsolved, actively-felt, manually-performed task.
searches.venue: IBM Mainframes / IBM Mainframe Forum / Pentaho forums (practitioner venue)

searches.query: RecordEditor "layout wizard" guess field boundaries fixed width file analyse columns tool Bruce Martin — plus direct fetch of jrecord.sourceforge.net/JRecord06.html and record-editor.sourceforge.net/Record09.htm
searches.result_summary: The only in-domain prior attempt found anywhere. RecordEditor (Bruce Martin) changelog: 'New field search Function which will look for fields in a fixed width file' (rel 0.69.1), 'Better support Unknown Format (New screen available which will try and work out the file format...)' (0.69.1), 'New FileWizard reader for use when the file is not recognized' (0.85). I fetched the JRecord Layout Wizard doc to check the strength of the claim: it is INTERACTIVE and MANUAL — 'To create a new field, click on the first column of the field' — the wizard colours alternating columns to help a human mark boundaries and then the human assigns types. So even this single in-domain effort is a hand-tool with a weak heuristic assist, not an automated inducer: no model, no evaluation, no benchmark, no published accuracy number.

searches.query: record layout inference fixed-width binary file machine learning neural (surfaced patents)
searches.result_summary: Three patents surfaced: US 10102260, US 10133802, US 10902013 — 'Method and apparatus for accelerated record layout detection' / 'accelerated data translation using record layout detection'. Reading the abstracts as surfaced: these operate on fixed-field data whose RECORD HEADERS CARRY a record length and a Layout ID, and provide hardware modules that dispatch to the matching known layout. That is layout SELECTION among registered layouts, in hardware, for throughput — not induction of an unknown layout from bytes. Not a competing effort, but recorded because it is the nearest thing to prior art in the patent literature.

searches.query: VLDB SIGMOD schema inference raw flat files data lake 2024 2025 fixed-width columns detection; digital preservation file format identification iPRES automatic characterisation unknown binary format
searches.result_summary: DB side: no VLDB/SIGMOD 2024-2025 paper on fixed-width column detection or flat-file layout induction. The DB community's raw-file work is CSV/delimited and text-table oriented (Pytheas-style table discovery, FlashProfile, Explain-Da-V, ALITE/schema matching, 'Visual Template Inference for Data Extraction from Documents' arXiv:2501.06659) — all assume delimiters or human-legible text. Preservation side: iPRES/DPC/PRONOM-DROID work is about IDENTIFYING WHICH known format a file is (signature matching against a registry) and 'significant properties'; the literature explicitly notes a methodological gap and has no work on inducing internal record structure of an unregistered fixed-width format. Both venues confirm the gap rather than fill it.
searches.venue: VLDB / SIGMOD (database — data wrangling venue) and iPRES (digital preservation)

serious_efforts.name: RecordEditor / JRecord 'FileWizard' + fixed-width field search (Bruce Martin)
serious_efforts.scale: Desktop tool, single file at a time; no dataset, no evaluation, no reported metric
serious_efforts.what_it_did: The only in-domain attempt found. An open-source flat-file/COBOL data editor with a 'field search function which will look for fields in a fixed width file', an 'Unknown Format' screen that 'will try and work out the file format', and a FileWizard reader for unrecognised files. I fetched the Layout Wizard documentation to test the claim: the wizard is interactive — it colours alternating columns and the user clicks the first column of each field and hand-assigns types. Heuristic assist for a human, not an automated inducer. No model, no benchmark, no published accuracy, no handling of REDEFINES/OCCURS DEPENDING ON.

serious_efforts.name: Binary protocol reverse engineering line: BinaryInferno / DynPRE / BinPRE / DL-ProS²
serious_efforts.scale: ~10 protocols, hand-labelled ground truth; nothing approaching 10^6 labelled units; no released large corpus
serious_efforts.what_it_did: ADJACENT DOMAIN, not in-domain. Infers field boundaries and some field semantics in undocumented binary NETWORK messages. BinaryInferno uses Shannon-entropy boundary detection plus atomic-type detectors (floats, timestamps), reaching precision 0.69 / recall 0.73. DynPRE probes a live server dynamically. BinPRE uses binary/instruction-level semantic similarity, reaching 0.73 format perfection and 0.74 semantic F1. DL-ProS² is U-Net + siamese + BiLSTM-CRF over traffic. All require network traffic and often a live endpoint or the client binary; all evaluate on ~10 hand-labelled protocols; none has a ground-truth generator, a scaling study, or any notion of EBCDIC/zoned/COMP-3/COMP encodings, record-length hypothesis search, or REDEFINES/OCCURS.

serious_efforts.name: PADS / LearnPADS / LearnPADS++ (Fisher, Walker, Zhu, White)
serious_efforts.scale: Handfuls of ad hoc formats; no labelled corpus released; not a learning-at-scale system
serious_efforts.what_it_did: The true intellectual ancestor: fully automatic inference of a PADS data description from positive examples of an ad hoc data source, then automatic generation of parsers and tools from that description; LearnPADS++ made it incremental for streaming/evolving sources. But it is MDL/chunking-based symbolic inference over tokenizable ASCII-ish records (web logs, Netstat output, CRT records), ~15 years old, with no learned model, no compute-scaling curve, and no mechanism for disambiguating packed-decimal vs zoned vs binary vs text at a given byte offset, no record-length hypothesis, no REDEFINES/OCCURS DEPENDING ON.
serious_efforts.year: 2008 (POPL, 'From dirt to shovels'), 2011 (ICDT, PADS project), 2012 (PADL, LearnPADS++)

g4_results.domain: ProcedureNet: recovering coded flight procedures and ARINC 424 legs from ADS-B trajectories
g4_results.g4_reasoning:
Fourteen searches across arXiv (export API + abs pages), GitHub (MCP repo and code search), HuggingFace (API), a benchmark/PwC sweep, and five domain-specific venues (OpenSky Symposium/Workshop and the traffic-library community, IEEE DASC, SESAR Innovation Days + ICRAT, Transportation Research Part C, MDPI Aerospace, plus the airport-noise-vendor practitioner space).

WHY NOT PASS. Two things block a clean PASS. (1) A mid-scale open dataset with exactly the headline label already exists: ATFMTraj on HuggingFace, confirmed via the HF API at 10K<n<100K trajectories, 5.93 GB, three airports, with arrival classes = runway x IAF x STAR and departure classes = SID. That is precisely 'which published procedure was flown', released, MIT-licensed, and paired with a 2024 method paper (ATSCC). (2) Counting adjacent-or-overlapping serious efforts gives four to five, not fewer than three: ATSCC/ATFMTraj (2024), the DASC 2022 holding/vectoring CNN which already feeds SID/STAR geometry into a network alongside the track and predicts the vectored-off flag, Kochenderfer's track+procedure deviation model (2023/AIAA JAIS 2025), the TRC 2022 RNAV pattern classifier, and an Aerospace 2026 clustering+knowledge-filter arrival-procedure detector. The field is not empty and it is moving — the 2026 Aerospace paper is evidence of active momentum in the last 12 months.

WHY NOT FAIL. The specific thesis is genuinely unoccupied on three axes, and the searches were unambiguous about it. First, ARINC 424 path-terminator leg inference does not exist anywhere: the arXiv API returned zero papers mentioning ARINC 424 / CIFP / path terminator in an ML context, and the web query for it returned only training courses, avionics manuals, and two patents running the FORWARD direction (coded leg -> rendered path). Nobody has published the inverse. Second, the CIFP-as-label-manufacturer bridge does not exist in open source at all: GitHub search_code for '"path terminator" "ADS-B"' returned total_count 0, and the nine ARINC 424 repos that exist are pure parsers with 0-12 stars, none of which touch a trajectory. Third, scale: every existing effort is one to three airports at 10^4 trajectories, hand-labelled; nothing is within two orders of magnitude of 10^6, and OpenSky's own derived flight tables carry no procedure label whatsoever.

The honest reading is that the naive framing ('classify which SID/STAR was flown from ADS-B') is partly occupied and demonstrably doable at small scale on an existing public dataset — a frontier-lab-free but not empty niche. The defensible framing is the part nobody has touched: per-timestep ARINC 424 path-terminator leg decomposition plus deviation attribution, with CIFP geometry as the free label manufacturer, scaled globally. If the study is narrowed to that, G4 is close to a PASS; as stated, with the procedure-ID headline, the ATFMTraj dataset and the DASC vectoring CNN make it MARGINAL. One caveat recorded rather than papered over: ScienceDirect (TRC 2022) and MDPI (Aerospace 2026) both returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch, so those two efforts' data scales and whether they use CIFP are unverified — if either turns out to be a large-scale CIFP-driven classifier this would move toward FAIL.
open_checkpoints: None found. No released model weights for procedure identification, procedure conformance, or ARINC 424 leg labelling from trajectories. The ATSCC paper (arXiv 2407.20028) released the ATFMTraj dataset but no pretrained trajectory encoder was located on HuggingFace or GitHub. GitHub search for ARINC 424 + ADS-B returned total_count 0 for both repositories and code.

g4_results.domain: Serial-crystallography indexing from sparse Bragg peak lists (peak point-set -> orientation/lattice matrix A, or "unindexable")
g4_results.g4_reasoning:
PASS, with two caveats that should be carried forward rather than ignored.

WHY PASS. Across 15 searches spanning general web, arXiv (full-text search UI), Europe PMC (three separate structured queries, 42 / 190 / 1570 hits inspected), GitHub repo + code search, HuggingFace datasets, Papers with Code, IUCr journals (domain venue 1), Structural Dynamics/ACA (domain venue 2) and CXIDB (domain data repository), I found ZERO serious efforts at the exact thesis: a learned model that maps a sparse monochromatic serial-crystallography Bragg peak list to an orientation/lattice matrix, trained on labels manufactured by running classical indexers over an archive. The decisive negative evidence is unusually clean:
  - arXiv contains exactly TWO papers matching "serial crystallography indexing", and neither uses learning.
  - Europe PMC's "SFX + ML + indexing" query returns 42 papers, and every single ML paper is hit/miss classification, data reduction, pixel-anomaly detection, peak finding, or peak integration. Not one indexer.
  - Europe PMC's "SFX + indexing rate / indexing algorithm" query returns 190 papers, and every indexing-algorithm paper (SPIND, SPIND-TC, XGANDALF, PINK, TORO, FINDEXER, MCDPS-SFX, Nasser et al.) is classical.
  - GitHub-wide search for "diffraction indexing neural network" returns exactly 2 repositories, both LaueNN by the same ESRF group, both Laue microdiffraction, one archived. Code search for serial-crystallography ML indexing returns 0.
  - No open labelled dataset exists at ANY scale, let alone 10^6. HuggingFace has literally nothing (the diffraction search returns a 6-row and a 5-row toy dataset). Papers with Code is defunct. CXIDB releases raw images, not (peak list -> A matrix) pairs. The labelled corpus this thesis needs does not exist and must be manufactured — which is exactly the FDM-1 structural pattern.
  - Independent third-party corroboration of the premise: FINDEXER (Struct. Dyn., Oct 2025, Sauter/Brewster at LBNL) states outright that ~50% of XFEL microcrystal samples fail the unit-cell-finding step. The failure tail is real and acknowledged in print by the field's own tool authors.

CAVEAT 1 — THE NEIGHBOURHOOD IS BUSY, JUST NOT WITH LEARNING. Four new CLASSICAL indexers landed in the last 18 months (TORO J. Appl. Cryst. 2024; FINDEXER Struct. Dyn. Oct 2025; Nasser/Poitevin/Dalton arXiv:2511.22875 Nov 2025; MCDPS-SFX Appl. Sci. 2026, which claims to more than double crystal yields on heterogeneous data). The white space is real but the baseline is moving fast, and any result must be measured against a 2026-vintage classical indexer, not against 2019 XGANDALF. Note especially that Poitevin and Dalton are SLAC ML-for-crystallography people who chose classical optimisation for this exact problem in Nov 2025 — either they evaluated and rejected learning, or a learned version is their next paper. That is the single largest scoop risk.

CAVEAT 2 — THE IDEA IS NOT NOVEL IN CRYSTALLOGRAPHY GENERALLY, ONLY IN THIS CELL. Learned indexing already exists in three neighbouring modalities: Laue microdiffraction (LaueNN, J. Appl. Cryst. 2022, and it is trained on SIMULATED spot geometry — the same shape-(c) manufacturer proposed here), powder XRD (JCIM 2025 and a transformer follow-up JCIM 2026), and EBSD/electron diffraction (Kaufmann Acta Mater. 2020; Latice VAE 2025; npj Comput. Mater. 2026). A reviewer will not be surprised by "learned indexer". The defensible novelty is specifically: sparse (15-200 peaks), monochromatic, unknown-orientation, potentially multi-lattice snapshot geometry at archive scale with pseudo-labels harvested from a classical indexer — none of the adjacent work does any of that.

SEPARATE FLAG, NOT G4 BUT MATERIAL: the proposal's claim that "peak arrays are already stored inside the CXI files, so the working corpus is sub-GB" is only PARTLY verified. The CXI format spec (v1.5+) does support inline peak lists, so many CXIDB deposits do carry compact peak arrays. But the specific 19M-image deposit CXIDB ID 185 is described on its landing page as raw AGIPD data plus calibration and geometry — I found no evidence that it ships peak lists or CrystFEL streams, and it is multi-TB. Under a 30GB-disk G6 constraint this must be checked deposit-by-deposit before the abundance claim is relied on; the sub-GB working corpus more likely comes from the CXI-format deposits plus locally-run peakfinder8 on a subset, or from simulation.
open_checkpoints: NO published checkpoint exists for indexing sparse serial-crystallography peak lists. Verified via GitHub repo search ('diffraction indexing neural network' returns exactly 2 repos, both Laue), GitHub code search (0 hits for '"serial crystallography" indexing "machine learning"'), and HuggingFace (0 relevant models/datasets).

ADJACENT ONLY — BM32ESRF/LaueNN (https://github.com/BM32ESRF/LaueNN): trainable/pretrained feed-forward hkl-recognition models for polychromatic Laue microdiffraction, per crystal system, trained on simulated spot geometry. 9 stars.
ADJACENT ONLY — ravipurohit1991/lauetoolsnn (https://github.com/ravipurohit1991/lauetoolsnn): Keras implementation of the same, now ARCHIVED. 7 stars.

NOT A CHECKPOINT — TORO (https://journals.iucr.org/j/issues/2024/04/00/jo5098/index.html) ships PyTorch code but has no learned weights; it is a classical optimiser expressed in PyTorch. Do not mistake this for prior learned art.
NOT INDEXING — PeakNet (arXiv:2303.15301) is a released U-Net for Bragg peak FINDING (image -> peak mask). It is an upstream complement to the proposed model, not a competitor.

searches.result_summary: Paley, Brewster, Mittan-Moreau & Sauter, 'FINDEXER: a new technique to find unit cells in sparse serial patterns', Structural Dynamics, Oct 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12585544/. Explicitly CLASSICAL (no NN, no training). Operates on spot-pair triples (q1,q2,theta). Independently confirms the premise: the authors state ~50% of XFEL microcrystal samples currently FAIL unit-cell finding. This is the strongest external corroboration of the failure-tail motivating the thesis — and it is being attacked classically, not with learning.
searches.venue: Structural Dynamics / PMC (domain venue #2: AIP/ACA serial-crystallography venue)

searches.query: diffraction indexing neural network
searches.result_summary: Exactly 2 repositories on all of GitHub: BM32ESRF/LaueNN (9 stars, https://github.com/BM32ESRF/LaueNN) and ravipurohit1991/lauetoolsnn (7 stars, ARCHIVED, https://github.com/ravipurohit1991/lauetoolsnn) — both the same authors, both polychromatic Laue microdiffraction of materials, not SFX. A parallel query 'serial crystallography indexing machine learning diffraction' returned total_count=0. Code search for '"serial crystallography" indexing "machine learning" language:python' returned 0. Code search for '"peakXPosRaw" indexing neural' returned 0.

searches.query: crystfel
searches.result_summary: 29 repos, all classical tooling: taw10/crystfel (the reference implementation), crystfelparser, crystfel_stream_parser, European-XFEL/CrystFEL-Jupyter-utilities, detwin. Confirms search is working (non-zero) and that no ML fork/extension of the indexing step exists publicly.

searches.query: datasets?search=crystallography and datasets?search=diffraction
searches.result_summary: crystallography: ascolda/ru_en_Crystallography_and_Spectroscopy (44.6k, text), mteb + vatolinalex wikipedia_crystallography (1.45k, text), ohlstrom/Crystallography-Open-Database-XRD-Patterns, LMucko/crystallography-open-database (533k structures, i.e. COD mirror — structures, NOT diffraction snapshots). diffraction: popoff4rtem/2D-Neutron-Diffraction-Dataset (6 rows), popoff4rtem/Diffraction-Dataset-For-Generative-Models (5 rows), aceengineer/digitalmodel-diffraction-rao (8.45k, marine hydrodynamics, irrelevant). ZERO peak-list / orientation-matrix datasets at any scale.

searches.query: crystallography indexing
searches.result_summary: paperswithcode.com is defunct — 302-redirects to huggingface.co/papers/trending. No benchmark, leaderboard, or task exists for diffraction-pattern indexing. Effectively n_relevant_hits 0.

searches.query: cxidb.org/browse.html and cxidb.org/id-185.html and cxidb.org/cxi.html
searches.result_summary: 246 deposits, of which ~120 are SFX. ID 185 = 'A multi-million image Serial Femtosecond Crystallography dataset collected at the European XFEL' (Sci. Data 2022, 10.1038/s41597-022-01266-w), CC0 public domain. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: the ID-185 landing page describes raw AGIPD data + calibration + geometry (agipd.geom, agipd_vds.geom); it does NOT advertise deposited CrystFEL stream files or extracted peak arrays, and the raw volume is multi-TB. Separately, the CXI format spec (cxidb.org/cxi.html) confirms 'This version of the CXI format adds support for peak lists, commonly used in crystallography' from v1.5, so many CXI-format SFX deposits DO carry compact peak arrays inline. No deposit anywhere is a released (peak list -> A matrix) labelled dataset.

Cryst. 2026, classical), 'Indexing of electron back-scatter diffraction patterns using a convolutional neural network' (Acta Materialia 2020, Kaufmann et al.), 'Latice' EBSD VAE (Cell Rep. Phys. Sci. Sep 2025, https://www.cell.com/cell-reports-physical-science/fulltext/S2666-3864(25)00470-9), 'Determining the grain orientations of battery materials from electron diffraction patterns using CNNs' (npj Comput. Mater. 2026, 10.1038/s41524-026-02002-3), 'Accelerating electron diffraction analysis using graph neural networks and attention mechanisms' (npj Comput. Mater. 2026). All are dense-image or polychromatic-Laue inputs from materials science; none is sparse monochromatic serial protein-crystal snapshot indexing.

searches.result_summary: Confirms DL in SFX is concentrated entirely UPSTREAM of indexing: PeakNet (arXiv 2303.15301, U-Net Bragg peak finding), 'End-to-end deep learning pipeline for real-time Bragg peak segmentation' (Front. High Perf. Comput. 2025, 10.3389/fhpcp.2025.1536471), robust peak finder (2021). No HuggingFace dataset exists for this domain at all.
searches.venue: web (general) — SFX ML landscape / peak-level DL

serious_efforts.name: LaueNN / lauetoolsnn (Purushottam Raj Purohit et al., ESRF BM32)
serious_efforts.scale: Tiny. Per-crystal-system models train in ~25 s (cubic) to ~15 min (triclinic). Synthetic training sets only. 9 + 7 GitHub stars.
serious_efforts.what_it_did: CLOSEST EXISTING WORK, adjacent modality. Feed-forward neural network that predicts hkl per diffraction spot from 1D features (distribution of mutual angles between a spot and its neighbours), then recovers orientation, for synchrotron Laue MICRODIFFRACTION of poly/single-crystalline materials. Training data manufactured by SIMULATION (shape (c)) per crystal system. Indexes in <1 s. This proves the 'spot-list -> hkl by NN' shape works and is CPU-trainable, but it is polychromatic white-beam Laue on materials, not sparse monochromatic serial snapshots of protein microcrystals, and it was never scaled beyond per-crystal-system synthetic training.

serious_efforts.name: Deep-learning powder XRD indexing (AIdex, JCIM 2025; transformer follow-up, JCIM 2026)
serious_efforts.scale: Simulated peak lists; scale not disclosed as a released dataset. No public checkpoint or dataset found.
serious_efforts.what_it_did: ADJACENT MODALITY, same abstract task. End-to-end prediction of extinction group + unit-cell parameters directly from powder-diffraction peak positions, all crystal systems, trained on simulated peaks. ~97% top-5 extinction-group accuracy, <5% MAPE on cell parameters. Input is a 1D peak list with NO orientation component and NO missing-reflection/multi-lattice pathology, so it does not touch the SFX problem, but it demonstrates the 'peaks -> cell by learned model' idea is already in the crystallography literature and moving fast (two papers in ~12 months).

serious_efforts.name: CNN/VAE indexing of EBSD and electron-diffraction patterns (Kaufmann et al. 2020; Latice 2025; battery-materials CNN 2026)
serious_efforts.scale: Simulated pattern libraries, typically 10^4-10^6 images; no released benchmark for the SFX task.
serious_efforts.what_it_did: ADJACENT MODALITY, well-established. CNNs and variational autoencoders map electron backscatter / STEM diffraction PATTERNS (dense 2D images) to Euler angles, trained on dynamically simulated patterns. Materials science, image input, single-lattice. Establishes 'learned orientation determination' as unremarkable to reviewers, but the input modality (dense image) and the physics are different, and none of this literature addresses the sparse-peak-list, unknown-cell, multi-lattice SFX regime.

serious_efforts.name: CLASSICAL competition in the exact target niche (not ML, but active): TORO 2024, FINDEXER Oct 2025, Nasser-Poitevin-Dalton Nov 2025, MCDPS-SFX 2026
serious_efforts.scale: Software releases, no learned parameters, no released training corpora.
serious_efforts.what_it_did: NOT learned methods, listed because they occupy the same problem and set a fast-moving baseline. TORO (J. Appl. Cryst. 2024) = PyTorch-implemented but hand-designed relaxed Laue score + robust optimisation. FINDEXER (Struct. Dyn. Oct 2025, LBNL/DIALS) = spot-pair (q1,q2,theta) unit-cell finding for sparse serial patterns; states ~50% of XFEL microcrystal samples fail cell-finding. Nasser, Poitevin & Dalton (arXiv:2511.22875, Nov 2025, SLAC) = symmetry-aware lattice decoding, explicitly targeting sparse patterns with few reflections, evaluated on CXIDB data. MCDPS-SFX (Appl. Sci. 2026) = reference-based multi-lattice indexing, reported to more than double crystal yields. Three new classical indexers in 18 months means the failure tail is recognised and under attack — a learned indexer must beat a target that is moving.

known_limitations: Two adversary agents reported their WebSearch quota exhausted (200/200) before issuing queries and fell back to direct arXiv/Europe PMC/HTTP fetches. Their G3 external-evidence coverage is therefore weaker than their on-box measurements. Recorded rather than smoothed over.
Two screened survivors (Headerless load-layout recovery, ProcedureNet) were cut by the top-4 finalist slice and were NOT adversarially tested in this round.
Serious-effort counts are the counting agents' judgement of what is 'serious'. The underlying paper/tool names and URLs are recorded so the count can be re-derived by a reader who disagrees.

method.adversary: 1 agent per finalist, default posture REJECT, tasked with G3 kill attempt, G1 licence reality, G2 degeneracy, G6 concrete feasibility
method.finalist_selection: g4_verdict != FAIL, sorted ascending by crowding score, top 4
method.g4: 1 agent per survivor, >=8 real searches across >=4 venues of which >=2 domain-specific, recording actual papers/URLs
method.screen: 1 screener applying G1/G2/G3/G6 and the pre-killed list, returning ranked survivors + gate-attributed rejections

rejected.killed_by: G3 (+ deduplicated into the blind-binary-structure family)
rejected.name: Schema-free decoding of self-delimiting binary serialisations (protobuf/Thrift/CBOR)
rejected.reason: Protobuf's wire format is partly self-describing, so a 200-line deterministic parser (protobuf-inspector, blackboxprotobuf, pbtk) already recovers tags and wire types with no model. What remains is the semantic layer ('this varint is a unix timestamp'), and a frontier model handed the deterministic parse tree as TEXT plausibly does that by plain prompting — the exact failure mode that killed the founder's previous project. Merged into the blind-structure family; CopybookLM is the better-specified survivor because EBCDIC/COMP-3 has no self-describing framing and the cross-record aggregation argument is not promptable.

rejected.name: Blind bit-level decoding of ASN.1 UPER / 3GPP control plane
rejected.reason: Every 3GPP ASN.1 schema is published and asn1c decodes exactly in microseconds, so the learned model is worthless for standard messages. Value collapses to vendor-proprietary extension containers and malformed PDUs, and the candidate could not name a deployed bitstream whose schema is undownloadable. A beautiful method with no patient. Also G1-weak: real public captures at 10^6 scale are unverified, so 'abundance' reduces to self-generated data.

rejected.name: Structural carving: offset-level layout parsing of opaque firmware and container blobs
rejected.reason: The label manufacturer is unblob/binwalk, which only labels formats it already has signatures for — so the model can only be supervised on the cases where the free tool already wins, and cannot be supervised on the unknown formats that are the entire value proposition. Synthetic composition partly patches this but cannot create realistic unknown-format texture. Separately, the adjacent framing (file-fragment type classification: FiFTy, the 2025 comprehensive survey, grayscale-image methods) is genuinely crowded, and an agentic model can call unblob in a loop.

rejected.name: Compile-time configuration recovery from binaries (Kconfig / ./configure / #ifdef)
rejected.reason: The scaling axis is BUILDS, not units: 10^8 function-level units all inherit one of only ~10^4 distinct label vectors, and you cannot run 10^6 kernel builds, so 'more data' plateaus at ~10^4 effective labels. On top of that, a large fraction of CONFIG options leave a greppable trace (exported symbol, printk string, /proc entry), so `strings | grep` plus a frontier model recovers much of the vector with zero training — bn-kconfig-recover already does this. The white space exists precisely because the task is capped.

rejected.name: Container image to build-instruction (Dockerfile) recovery
rejected.reason: Severe on two fronts. Most public images still carry history[] metadata, so the 'recovery' is a metadata read that dfimage/whaler do in 20 lines. For squashed images the filesystem is self-describing — hand a frontier model /var/lib/dpkg/status or the top-level listing and it reconstructs the apt-get lines by plain reasoning. The input (file paths, package names) is human-legible text, which the mission flags as the reject condition. Only multi-stage structure and instruction ORDER survive, which is a much smaller thesis.

rejected.name: FPGA bitstream to LUT/route configuration recovery
rejected.reason: The killer is not a language model, it is a fuzzer: Project X-Ray's differential fuzzing solves the bit-to-feature mapping EXACTLY for any family where you can run the vendor tool — and for families where you cannot fuzz, you also cannot generate training labels. The moat and the data source are the same wall. G4 is borderline-failing anyway (Debit, BIL, Bit2ncd, fasm2bels, the 2026 silicon-to-netlist SoK, plus >3 serious efforts overall), and G6 is marginal because nextpnr P&R is seconds-to-minutes per design, capping generation around 10^5.

rejected.name: Synthesis-recipe provenance from gate-level netlists
rejected.reason: There is no existing abundant corpus at all — every (netlist, recipe) pair must be synthesised by running yosys, so this is pure data manufacture with no 'abundant data that exists but is unlabelled', breaking the first part of the FDM-1 pattern. Generation of 10^6 units is 1-3 CPU-days at the edge of feasibility. G3 is also leaky (technology library is literally in the cell names, forcing an artificial anonymisation step a reviewer will call out) and the buyer story is IP-litigation, which is small and slow.

rejected.name: Profile-free object and type layout recovery from memory images
rejected.reason: No existing abundant corpus: public labelled memory dumps are CTF-scale, so every unit must be manufactured by dumping processes you built yourself. G3 then compounds it: when the profile matches, Volatility parses exactly and free; when it does not, pool-tag and allocator-metadata heuristics already recover most kernel objects. DeepMem (CCS 2018) demonstrated gains and saw essentially no adoption — a strong market signal that the pain is not acute. Eval is circular too: ground truth requires symbols, but the customer's binaries have none.

rejected.name: Argo float CTD calibration inversion (real-time to delayed-mode)
rejected.reason: The label is a human expert judgement produced largely by running a published deterministic algorithm (OWC weighted least squares against reference climatology), so a learned model is distilling a free tool — the same defect that kills the music-engraving candidate ('just run pyowc'). The expert labels are inconsistent across DACs, so scale buys more expert noise, and ~90% of floats need no adjustment in their first two years, making the positive class rare and the curve likely flat. G4 was never checked and ML-for-Argo-QC literature plausibly exists. Painful to cut — the corpus (2M profiles shipping raw and expert-adjusted values in the same NetCDF file) is genuinely beautiful.

rejected.name: Slicer inversion: process parameters and layer geometry from FFF G-code
rejected.reason: Most of the 40-dimensional target is recoverable by a 20-line deterministic script: layer height is the Z delta, temperature is literally M104, acceleration is M204, extrusion width follows from E per unit distance over layer height. A frontier model that writes that script beats a trained network on the majority of the vector, and the genuinely hidden residue (infill pattern class, slicer identity, seam strategy) is small and low-value.

rejected.name: Gerber-to-schematic: recovering design intent from PCB fabrication data
rejected.reason: G1 is self-declared PARTIAL — no verified >=10^6 corpus of real public board designs, only synthesis via auto-place-and-route. G3 then fails twice: net connectivity is already deterministically extractable by mature CAM tools, and component VALUE is physically undetermined by copper alone (two identical 0402 pads can be 100nF or 1nF), so the ceiling is set by missing information rather than compute. A frontier vision model on a rendered board with silkscreen recovers most of the remaining semantics with zero training.

rejected.name: Distribution-grid phase and topology inversion from meter voltage series
rejected.reason: The 10^6-scale corpus is NREL SMART-DS, which is entirely simulated — the real labelled AMI corpus is low 10^4 households, so there is no abundant real unlabelled data to pseudo-label. If OpenDSS scenarios do not reproduce real meter noise, clock skew and missing reads, more synthetic data actively makes the model worse: a scaling curve that bends the wrong way. Phase identification is also largely solved by voltage correlation plus spectral clustering and is already sold by AMI vendors.

rejected.killed_by: G2 (label is another model's output) + G4 (incumbent)
rejected.name: Grid frequency waveform inversion: system inertia and generation mix
rejected.reason: The 'ground truth' inertia is NESO's own model estimate, not a measurement — true inertia is never observed — so the study would be distilling somebody else's heuristic and is capped by it. That is not a free-truth environment. G4 also fails: GE Vernova already sells NESO an Effective Inertia Metering and Forecasting product and NESO has deployed ML inertia forecasting. Label diversity is capped at ~6 years x a handful of TSOs regardless of window count.

rejected.name: PV system parameter inversion from AC power time series
rejected.reason: This is a well-posed physics fit, and open tools already do it: pvlib plus least squares, NREL Solar-Data-Tools / PVInsight system profiler. A frontier model with a code interpreter writes the fit in twenty lines and, unlike a learned model, generalises to any array geometry. Beating a correct physical model is a bad bet. G1 also fails on independent-system count: the verified anchor is 1,287 systems (ANU), and system-days are not independent units.

rejected.name: Blind spectral unmixing from raw cytometry event clouds
rejected.reason: G1 fails on the honest unit: 211,359 public FCS files is two-thirds of an order of magnitude short of 10^6, and redefining the unit as an event-block is a gate-evasion rather than abundance. G3 then fails on identifiability — blind unmixing is determined only up to scaling and permutation without anchors, so a learned model may be structurally unable to beat a two-tube protocol change, and lab protocol plus regulatory guidance MANDATE the single-stain controls that make the problem moot. AutoSpill already ships inside FlowJo.

rejected.name: LC-MS instrument-state inversion from raw peak lists
rejected.reason: White space is already thin: mzRefinery and mzRecal recalibrate from identified peptides and MassShiftNet is a self-supervised neural mass-recalibration framework — at or over the three-serious-efforts threshold before the study starts. Modern instruments also carry hardware lock-mass keeping drift at 1-2 ppm, so the remaining headroom may be worth nothing, and if you must run a search engine to make labels, the customer can run one too.

rejected.name: Rietveld pre-solve: instrument-profile and microstructure inversion from powder diffraction
rejected.reason: Self-declared failure and correctly so: SimXRD-4M (ICLR 2025) is an open 4-million-pattern benchmark over 119,000 structures under 33 experimental conditions, and a 2019 Nat. Commun. work trained on 1,785,405 synthetic patterns. 'No open dataset at target scale' is simply false, and deep-learning XRD phase-ID papers are numerous. Rietveld refinement is also a mature well-conditioned optimiser, so the marginal value of a learned pre-solve is small.

rejected.name: Wireline log harmonisation: inverting tool, vendor and borehole effects
rejected.reason: Most of the label is literally in the LAS header (service company, tool mnemonics, run date, mud properties), so the recovery task is unnecessary wherever the header survives — the answer is in the artifact. The other half, curve reconstruction, is crowded: SPWLA/SPE/FORCE-2020 ML contests with public leaderboards have run for years. Petrophysicists also have deterministic chart-book corrections that are defensible to a regulator in a way a neural net is not.

rejected.name: Battery electrochemical parameter inversion from cycling curves
rejected.reason: Self-declared and confirmed: the largest public full-cycle dataset is ~180 cells (Severson/Attia MATR) with ~10^5 cycles across all major archives — two to four orders of magnitude short of 10^6 independent units, with CALCE adding ~15 cells. PyBaMM simulation is unlimited but is manufactured data with only ~180 real cells to validate against, making the scaling study self-referential and the sim-to-real gap unverifiable.

rejected.name: CRS-Recover: projection/datum identification from bare coordinate arrays
rejected.reason: Exhaustive search kills it: enumerate the ~10^3-10^4 CRSs in proj.db, inverse-project, and score each hypothesis against a coastline raster — cheap, exact, interpretable, and better than a small learned model on the easy 90%. A frontier model with a code interpreter writes that search, which is 'plain prompting eats it' at system level. Worse, the claimed moat (custom local grids NOT in EPSG) is exactly where you also cannot generate labels, because pyproj can only manufacture labels for CRSs already in proj.db. Same circularity that killed the firmware-carving candidate.

rejected.killed_by: G3 (+ G4 partly compromised; deduplicated with ShapeInverse)
rejected.name: GlyphMap: Unicode codepoint recovery from vector glyph outlines
rejected.reason: One draw() call away from death: rasterise the outline to a 64x64 bitmap, hand it to any frontier vision model, and it reads the character today with plain prompting and no training, for Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, CJK and most Indic. The thesis reduces to a residue (PUA, corporate icon fonts) that may be tiny. G4 is also partly compromised — SVG-Fonts is an open 14M-example vector-glyph dataset and vector-font transformers (DeepVecFont, VecFontSDF, arXiv 2502.00250) mean vector-glyph modelling is not white space.

rejected.name: Engraver: music engraving layout-decision prediction from symbolic score
rejected.reason: Near-fatal and trivial: if you want a layout, run the engraver. LilyPond and Verovio are free, deterministic, and better than any small model, and a frontier model with a shell just invokes them — a model that imitates LilyPond has zero reason to exist. The surviving reframing (learning a specific publisher's house style from scanned plates) moves ground truth from free shape-(c) to scarce shape-(a) on scanned images, breaking G1, G2 and G6 at once. Also sits close to OMR, which is crowded.

rejected.name: FieldOps: inverse dynamics for farm management events from field spectral time series
rejected.reason: This is precisely the founder's previous death, transplanted: geospatial foundation models (Prithvi, Clay, AlphaEarth-style embeddings) are trained on all of Sentinel/Landsat and explicitly marketed as 'fine-tune on 50 labelled fields for any task'. If a frontier EO model plus a linear probe on the same tiny seed matches the pseudo-labelling pipeline, the thesis dies — and those models get better every year. G4 is also borderline (conservation-tillage and cover-crop detection from Sentinel-2 is an active applied literature with carbon-MRV framing), and farmer-reported tillage labels are noisy enough to flatten the curve for reasons unrelated to the thesis.

rejected.name: TimetableInduction: manufacturing GTFS schedules from raw transit vehicle GPS
rejected.reason: Classical pipelines already exist and are cheap (gps2gtfs, busbuzzard; DBSCAN-plus-HMM stop detection is a textbook baseline), and a frontier model with a code interpreter writes a competent version in one shot. Worse, the free-label distribution is ontologically wrong for the target: agencies publishing GTFS-RT are formal, funded, fixed-route and paved-road, while the intended beneficiaries (matatus, jeepneys, colectivos) have no fixed stops or schedules — pseudo-labelling transfers badly across that gap. G5 is also thin: development agencies and small vendors, not deep pockets.

rejected.name: MojibakeChain: recovering multi-hop encoding-corruption chains
rejected.reason: Brute force wins: the codec vocabulary is tens of entries and chains are short, so enumerating all chains up to length 3, inverting each and scoring with a character n-gram model runs in milliseconds with no training — which is what ftfy's fix_and_explain already does for Latin cases. A frontier model can both write that brute-forcer and read common Latin-1/UTF-8 mojibake directly. The residue (CJK legacy chains ftfy explicitly refuses, lossy chains) is real but small, and the economic tail is thin: library catalogue migration is a one-off, low-budget purchase.

rejected.name: DissectorNet: binary protocol field-structure induction from raw packet bytes
rejected.reason: Automatic protocol reverse engineering is an established sub-field far beyond three serious efforts: Netzob, Nemesys, NETPLIER (NDSS 2021), BinPRE, arXiv 2301.03584 (field type classification for unknown binary protocols), arXiv 2301.03585 (PCA segmentation refinement), arXiv 2412.02540 (state-machine inference) — several of which already use tshark as ground truth, i.e. the exact proposed label manufacturer. The only differentiator left ('nobody ran the supervised-at-scale version') is too thin to fund.

rejected.name: VoyageFuel: per-voyage fuel and emissions from AIS with the EU MRV seed
rejected.reason: The supervision is one scalar per ship-year (THETIS-MRV annual verified totals for ships >5000 GT), so the effective label count is ~10^4-10^5 no matter how many AIS rows you hold — the scaling curve is capped by label information rather than data volume, which is exactly the failure this study is designed to detect and a bad way to spend it. Physics is also a strong training-free baseline: admiralty coefficient / cube law plus a published SFOC, or Holtrop-Mennen with a weather correction, is the industry standard and may sit inside the noise floor of the aggregate labels.

rejected.name: TableInverse: recovering the source query behind published statistical tables
rejected.reason: In the real world the headers are right there. Give a frontier model the table WITH its row and column labels and it identifies the source variables immediately by plain prompting, so the header-free framing is artificial — and an artificial framing is a fatal tell for a funding thesis. The defensible reframings (table linkage, disclosure-risk auditing) are a different and smaller thesis, and reconstruction attacks on published tables are already a studied area in statistical disclosure control, so white space is not assured either.

rejected.name: ShapeInverse: inverting OpenType text shaping for complex scripts
rejected.reason: The environment inverts itself in the exact deployment setting: PDFs embed their fonts, so an engineer (or a frontier model with a code tool) enumerates candidate strings, re-shapes each with HarfBuzz and the same font, and matches — with a character n-gram model and beam search that is a training-free solver for a large fraction of cases. The moat shrinks to fonts subsetted beyond usefulness or unavailable. Also close enough to the already-killed PDF text-extraction / document-OCR cluster that reviewers will lump it in, and for scripts with available glyph shapes rasterise-and-VLM short-circuits it again. Deduplicated with GlyphMap; both die on the same reasoning.

survivors.g1_corpus: Assemblage corpus (arXiv 2405.03991): 428,884 Linux ELF + 890,000 Windows PE binaries built from 30,856 GitHub repos with recorded build configs. Plus distro debug-symbol archives, free and bulk-downloadable: deb.debian.org/debian-debug, debuginfod.debian.net, Ubuntu ddebs, Fedora debuginfod (Debian bookworm alone: 64,419 binary packages / 34,790 source packages). Unit = function-with-CU-label; a mid-size binary has 10^3-10^4 functions, so >=10^7 labelled units is conservative.
survivors.g2_mechanism: DWARF is the structured source that still exists. .debug_info records, for free, the compile unit each function came from (DW_TAG_compile_unit ranges, DW_AT_decl_file) and which regions are inlined callees. Manufacture: download a debuginfo binary, walk DWARF with pyelftools to get the exact CU partition, then `objcopy --strip-all` and keep the stripped bytes as input. Milliseconds per unit, no human, no seed model. Critically there is NO circularity: the labels come from the symbol table, not from the heuristic tool that is the baseline.
survivors.g3_argument: The label is a partition over thousands of functions expressed over byte offsets in a multi-megabyte binary. There is no prompt that expresses it and no context window that holds it. Scale monotonicity is physical: each additional distro release / architecture / compiler generation adds a new linker layout regime (section ordering, --gc-sections, LTO partitioning, identical-code-folding, PGO reordering) and the model's job is exactly to learn the joint distribution over those regimes. The regimes that break the trivial baseline (LTO, ICF, BOLT/PGO reordering) are the ones becoming MORE common over time, so the thesis gets stronger as toolchains improve rather than weaker as models improve.

survivors.g5_buyer: Binary SBOM / software-composition-analysis vendors (FOSSA, Finite State, ONEKEY, NetRise) who must attribute a CVE to the specific vendored object file inside a stripped firmware blob rather than to the whole image — a requirement being hardened by the EU Cyber Resilience Act's firmware SBOM obligations.
survivors.input_modality: Raw machine-code byte windows (512-2048B) plus address-ordered relocation/xref/call-graph features from a stripped ELF/PE. Not disassembly prose, not text.
survivors.name: Inverse Linking: compile-unit partitioning of stripped binaries
survivors.one_line: Given a stripped executable's raw code bytes, recover the object-file (compile-unit) partition it was linked from, plus a coarse source-identity class per unit.
survivors.output_label: Per-function compile-unit id (a partition over the binary's functions), CU count, CU boundary offsets, coarse source-file/namespace class per unit.
survivors.why_survives: Best-balanced candidate: verified 10^7-scale legally-obtainable corpus, a zero-cost exact label manufacturer with no circularity, a label shape that is literally inexpressible as a prompt, thin verified white space (REcover's own abstract says the problem 'has not been sufficiently studied'), a named buyer under regulatory pressure, and an ideal CPU profile. The one real risk to design around is the address-contiguity baseline — the study must report boundary F1 against 'every contiguous run is one unit' and must weight the eval toward LTO/ICF/reordered binaries. Note adjacency to the headerless-firmware candidate below: same corpus, different label; do not run both as one study.

survivors.g1_corpus: The streams already exist in the billions: Software Heritage holds 27 billion unique source files from 421 million projects; Govdocs1 is ~1 million freely redistributable documents (digitalcorpora.org); every .deb/.whl/.jar/.apk/PNG/ZIP in the Debian archive (64,419 packages) contains DEFLATE streams. Plaintext feedstock for labelled generation is unbounded from the same sources; 10^6 labelled streams is minutes of CPU.
survivors.g2_mechanism: The compressor is the oracle. Take any byte string, run it through ~10 encoder implementations x ~10 levels x ~4 strategies and you have ~400 perfectly labelled streams per input at microsecond cost. The label is genuinely NOT in the artifact: raw DEFLATE has no header at all, and zlib's FLEVEL field is 2 advisory bits that are routinely wrong or absent — so this is a real inverse problem, not metadata reading. Ground truth is exact and free forever, and every new encoder release extends the label set at zero cost.
survivors.g3_argument: The input is a maximum-entropy bitstream whose signal lives in block-split boundaries, Huffman table shapes, match-length/distance histograms and lazy-matching tie-break artefacts. Plain prompting is not merely weak, it is inexpressible — there is no legible text. Discriminating two encoders that differ only in match-finder tie-breaking is a pure statistical problem that gets strictly easier with more streams and more content diversity, and a frontier model getting bigger does not move it at all because the modality is wrong. The framing must be forensic (carved/truncated fragments, plaintext unavailable, encoders outside the candidate set) so the brute-force recompression oracle is not the comparison.

survivors.input_modality: Raw compressed bitstream bytes (Huffman/ANS-coded, near-maximum entropy). Categorically outside any text pretraining distribution; a text tokenizer destroys the signal by construction.

survivors.one_line: From the entropy-coded bytes of a DEFLATE/zstd/brotli/LZMA stream, identify the encoder implementation, version bucket and parameter tuple — precisely enough to recompress byte-identically.

survivors.why_survives: Strongest G3 modality argument in the entire pool — a frontier model literally cannot represent the input — combined with the cheapest label manufacturer and the best G6 profile (generate, featurise, discard; disk pressure ~zero). Verified white space: only algorithm-FAMILY detection exists (arXiv 2111.09034, FiFTy-style fragment typing), nothing at implementation/parameter granularity. The known kill (recompress-and-compare when you hold the plaintext) is real but bounded, and the study must headline the fragment/no-plaintext setting where that oracle does not exist.

survivors.g1_corpus: Maven Central, publicly and bulk-downloadable. A 2025 Zenodo extraction covers >=16.5 million POMs; mvnrepository reports ~69 million indexed artifacts (single source, unverified); a 2025 dataset covers 122,201 artifacts released in one calendar year. Unit = a .class file and a typical jar holds 10^2-10^3 classes, so even the conservative single-year slice gives >10^7 class-level units.
survivors.g2_mechanism: The jar carries its own answer key and you delete it. META-INF/MANIFEST.MF records Created-By, Build-Jdk, Build-Jdk-Spec, Build-Tool; maven-archiver writes pom.properties. Strip those files, keep the bytecode, and you have a perfectly labelled pair at zero marginal cost, 10^7 times over. Secondary manufacturer for rare versions: recompile source-available projects under a matrix of JDKs in Docker.
survivors.g3_argument: The target is a point version (javac 11.0.2 vs 11.0.9) and a flag set, distinctions invisible to reasoning and visible only in codegen micro-quirks — constant-pool entry ordering, when a synthetic accessor is emitted, StackMapTable frame-compression choices. That is an empirical fingerprint whose resolution improves monotonically with the number of (artifact, toolchain) pairs; more versions in the label set means finer discrimination, not confusion. A bigger general model has no path to these quirks because they are not described anywhere in text — the field's own consensus is that the task is impossible.

Corpus is enormous, legally obtainable and self-labelling; G6 is excellent. Mandatory reframing to survive G3: the class-file version bytes leak the -target JDK for free, so the headline must be tamper/inconsistency detection (bytecode vs declared manifest), not 'guess the JDK', and the eval must include artifacts whose -source/-target decouples class-file version from actual compiler.

survivors.g1_corpus: Manufactured by deletion from binaries that already exist: Assemblage (428,884 Linux ELF + 890,000 Windows PE, arXiv 2405.03991) is already >10^6 units before any cross-compilation; Debian bookworm's 64,419 packages across ~8 architectures; plus cross-compilation of Software Heritage sources to 20+ long-tail ISAs (RISC-V, Xtensa, ARC, MIPS variants). Real vendor firmware images reserved as held-out eval.
survivors.g2_mechanism: The header IS the label, so you manufacture the task by deleting it. Read an ELF/PE's true load address, entry point, architecture and section table with pyelftools, then strip all headers and optionally relocate the image to a random base — you now have a headerless blob whose every answer you know exactly. Cost: one header read plus one memcpy per unit. The cleanest manufacturer in the pool: the labels already sit inside 10^6+ public artefacts and no tool, model or human is in the loop.
survivors.g3_argument: Base-address recovery is a global inverse over the whole blob: the correct base is the one under which the largest number of embedded 32/64-bit words become valid pointers into strings, code and tables. No prompt formulation exists, no context window holds 8MB, and the input has no text. Scaling is monotone and directly testable: coverage of more architectures, ABIs and compiler pointer-emission idioms strictly improves generalisation to an unseen vendor blob, and the long-tail ISAs are exactly where existing tools have nothing at all.

survivors.g1_corpus: Real side (shape c): government and academic fixed-width public-use data files that still ship their published record layouts — US Census PUMS and historical microdata, IPUMS, CPS, NHANES, IRS SOI, CMS Medicare public-use files, and the ICPSR archive's tens of thousands of studies distributed as fixed-width ASCII with SAS/SPSS setup files that ARE the layouts. NARA electronic records add archival holdings. Records are the unit and a single microdata file yields 10^6-10^8, so >=10^6 units is trivially cleared; layout diversity in the real half is the honest limit and must be measured. Synthetic side unbounded via GnuCOBOL / Cobrix serialisers.
survivors.g2_mechanism: Shape (b): a COBOL serialiser is a deterministic environment supplying exact ground truth — generate a random copybook (field order, PIC clauses, COMP-3/COMP/DISPLAY, sign conventions, OCCURS DEPENDING ON), serialise real tabular data through it, and you get byte streams with exact per-byte field boundaries at zero marginal cost. Shape (c): the public fixed-width files above were generated from layouts that are still published, giving free real (bytes, layout) pairs to calibrate the synthetic distribution and to measure the sim-to-real gap before anything else is done.
survivors.g3_argument: The signal is byte-level statistics — nibble distributions of packed decimal, sign nibbles C/D/F, EBCDIC digit runs 0xF0-0xF9, alignment periodicity, high-order-byte entropy of binary integers — and crucially it becomes identifiable only by integrating evidence ACROSS 10^5 records of the same file, which no context window holds and no prompt expresses. A frontier model handed a 2KB hex dump degrades within a few hundred bytes and cannot aggregate at all; making the model bigger does not change that, because the bottleneck is cross-record aggregation over a non-text modality, not reasoning.

Two honest weaknesses the study must confront: (i) the abundant real corpus is ASCII fixed-width while the high-value target is EBCDIC with packed decimal, so the sim-to-real gap must be measured on the public files FIRST; (ii) entropy/periodicity change-point detection is a strong training-free baseline on simple layouts, so the eval must weight REDEFINES, mixed record types and packed fields with no separators.

survivors.g1_corpus: OpenSky Network historical ADS-B: >30 trillion messages from >5000 sensors, free research access via Impala/Trino plus published derived flight tables in the 10^8 range. FAA Coded Instrument Flight Procedures (CIFP) in ARINC 424 v18 is a free public download refreshed every 28 days; Eurocontrol/EAD and open AIXM extend coverage; open parsers exist (github.com/rstory1/parseCifp). >=10^6 flight trajectories is comfortably reachable.
survivors.g2_mechanism: The literal VPT structure. Shape (c) first: CIFP gives the exact geometric definition of every published leg for free, so deterministic geometric matching labels the clean, on-procedure flights at zero cost — this is the 40k contractor hours. Then shape (a): train an inverse model on that exactly-labelled seed (densified with BlueSky/X-Plane simulator trajectories flying coded procedures under randomised wind and aircraft type) and pseudo-label the vastly larger corpus of messy real trajectories — vectored arrivals, partial procedures, missed approaches — that the geometric matcher rejects. That is the 11M hours.
survivors.g3_argument: The input is a numeric flight path; there is no natural-language expression of the task and no frontier model ingests trajectory tensors natively. The value lives entirely in the tail the deterministic matcher throws away, and that tail is exactly what the pseudo-labelling loop expands into: more flights, more airports, more weather regimes, more aircraft types and more 28-day CIFP cycles all increase coverage of procedure variants and off-nominal executions. The prior being learned — what a vectored downwind that rejoins at the FAF looks like versus a full published transition — is empirical and cannot be prompted into existence.

Two execution risks to budget explicitly: (i) a well-tuned DTW/Frechet matcher with a Viterbi leg decode is a strong training-free baseline, so the eval must be weighted to vectored and off-procedure flights; (ii) procedures change every 28 days, so historical CIFP-cycle alignment is a data-engineering trap that could dominate the error budget if not handled from day one. Acquisition (OpenSky query time), not training, is the compute risk.

survivors.g1_corpus: Coherent X-ray Imaging Data Bank (cxidb.org), open deposits — notably CXIDB ID 185, 'A multi-million image Serial Femtosecond Crystallography dataset collected at the European XFEL' (Sci. Data 2022), ~19 million images released explicitly for algorithm development, plus dozens of other SFX/SSX deposits. Crystallography Open Database provides 534,680 structures for unlimited simulated peak lists. Peak arrays are already stored inside the CXI files, so the working corpus is sub-GB.
survivors.g2_mechanism: Shape (b), and it is the VPT move with an algorithm standing in for the contractors: run free classical indexers (CrystFEL with XGANDALF/MOSFLM/TORO, DIALS) across the archive — every pattern they DO index becomes a free exact (peak list -> A-matrix) pair at pure CPU cost with no human in the loop. Shape (c) for the failure tail: forward-simulate peak lists from COD/PDB cells with sampled orientation, mosaicity, partiality, detector gaps and shot noise, which manufactures labelled examples of exactly the pathologies that make real patterns unindexable.
survivors.g3_argument: The input is a set of 40 pixel coordinates; prompting a language model with it is not a coherent operation, and no larger general model changes that. Classical indexers are per-pattern combinatorial searches that amortise nothing across a run; a learned indexer accumulates priors over cells, orientations and detector pathologies, so indexing yield rises monotonically with patterns seen and compute spent. Indexing rate is the literal throughput bottleneck of the field — facilities discard the majority of their hits — so the metric that improves with scale is the metric the customer buys.

survivors.why_survives: Deliberately unfashionable, verified 10^7-scale open corpus explicitly released for algorithm development, compact units that make the CPU ladder trivial, and a buyer whose cost function is beamtime — the most expensive unit of anything on this list. Unlike the Argo and music-engraving candidates it is not distillation of a free tool: the training labels come from the patterns the tool solves, but the TARGET is the disjoint population it fails on. The honest open question the study must answer first is what fraction of unindexed patterns are information-limited (too few peaks) versus algorithm-limited (multi-lattice, bad geometry, unusual cell) — measure that split before committing.
